members.statement: In a graded lipid-peroxidation series, the sub-350 nm photon flux scales as the square of the 400-500 nm triplet-carbonyl photon flux (log-log slope 2.0 +/- 0.3), because sub-350 nm quanta require pairwise pooling of two carbonyl excitations rather than any single catalogued chemiexcitation step.

hypothesis.statement: In a graded lipid-peroxidation series, the sub-350 nm photon flux scales as the square of the 400-500 nm triplet-carbonyl photon flux (log-log slope 2.0 +/- 0.3), because sub-350 nm quanta require pairwise pooling of two carbonyl excitations rather than any single catalogued chemiexcitation step.

scope.population: Cell-free aqueous linoleic-acid / phosphatidylcholine liposome suspension undergoing Fe(II)/H2O2-initiated peroxidation, and in parallel Chlamydomonas reinhardtii suspensions dosed with exogenous linoleic acid, both in 1 cm quartz cuvettes at 25 C, air-saturated
scope.condition: At least six initiator doses spanning a 100-fold range of total emission intensity, each measured simultaneously in two calibrated bands: 260-340 nm and 400-500 nm
scope.comparator: The same preparation at the lowest initiator dose; and the alternative model in which sub-350 nm emission is the short-wave tail of the same single-step chemiexcitation (predicting slope 1.0)
scope.outcome: beta = d(log absolute photon flux 260-340 nm)/d(log absolute photon flux 400-500 nm), fitted across the dose series with band-specific absolute calibration

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: beta is statistically indistinguishable from 1.0 (95% CI containing 1.0 and excluding 2.0), i.e. the UV band tracks the visible band proportionally and therefore shares its single-quantum origin (or is filter leakage); equivalently, the sub-340 nm band is undetectable at every dose so beta is undefined.
hypothesis.estimand: beta, the log-log slope of absolute 260-340 nm flux on absolute 400-500 nm flux; decision thresholds beta<1.3 refutes, beta>1.7 supports.

rationale.step: The field states its own UPE band as ~350-1300 nm and locates the unexplained region at wavelengths shorter than 350 nm, i.e. the mechanistic gap opens exactly at the short-wave edge of the band the field can account for.

The catalogued ROS chemiexcitation scheme terminates in triplet excited carbonyls from cyclic (1,2-dioxetane) and linear (tetroxide) high-energy intermediates, and the emission window assigned to excited carbonyl species is 350-550 nm; homogenate chemiluminescence spectra resolve five bands whose shortest is 420-450 nm, with nothing catalogued below 420 nm.

Photon energy in kcal/mol equals 28591 divided by wavelength in nm. The short-wave edge of the carbonyl band, 350 nm, is therefore 81.7 kcal/mol; this is the maximum single-quantum energy the catalogued chemistry delivers. 300 nm needs 95.3, 280 nm needs 102.1, 250 nm needs 114.4 and 190 nm needs 150.5 kcal/mol - all above that ceiling. Two pooled carbonyl quanta cap at 163.4 kcal/mol, i.e. a shortest accessible wavelength of 28591/163.4 = 175 nm, which brackets the entire historically claimed 190-250 nm band. Pairwise pooling is thus the minimal mechanism that reaches the unexplained region, and the only one that reaches it without new chemistry.

A pooling channel is second order in the excited-state population [T] while direct carbonyl emission is first order, so R_UV / R_vis is proportional to [T] and R_UV is proportional to R_vis squared; the log-log slope of UV on visible flux is therefore 2, independent of the reaction order of the primary chemistry that sets [T].

The estimand is deliberately UV flux against visible flux, not against substrate, because the primary chemistry is itself already known to be non-linear: low-level chemiluminescence in Fe-induced peroxidation of mitochondrial and microsomal membranes goes as the square of accumulated lipid hydroperoxide. Regressing band on band cancels that primary order out.

Linoleic-acid dosing of a living cell suspension is an established, graded UPE-generating perturbation in this corpus, and rat-tissue hydroperoxide dosing produces graded chemiluminescence with quantified lipid-peroxidation endpoints, so the dose series is a known-good preparation rather than a new one.

The prediction has an immediate corollary that discriminates it from the register's H4a: the UV percentage of total UPE is not a constant but rises with total intensity, which reconciles the historical report that a definite UV component of 20-40% appeared specifically during periods of active growth.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Build a two-channel photon counter: a quartz/MgF2 collection train from a 1 cm quartz cuvette, split by a 380 nm dichroic into (a) a cooled UV-extended bialkali or CsTe PMT behind a 260-340 nm interference filter and (b) a cooled bialkali PMT behind a 400-500 nm interference filter, both absolutely calibrated per band against a traceable low-flux standard so that counts convert to photons/s/cm2. Run a six-to-eight point Fe(II)/H2O2 dose series on linoleic-acid liposomes and, separately, an exogenous-linoleic-acid dose series on Chlamydomonas, spanning 100-fold in 400-500 nm flux. At each dose acquire both bands simultaneously for >=600 s. Interleave blanked controls (heat-killed sample, buffer only, filter-swapped) at every dose to bound leakage. Fit log(UV flux) against log(visible flux) by orthogonal-distance regression and report beta with its 95% CI. Repeat with the UV filter replaced by a matched blocked filter to quantify out-of-band leakage as an explicit additive term in the fit.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Two-channel cooled photon-counting PMT bench with quartz/MgF2 optics: UV-extended bialkali or CsTe photocathode with 260-340 nm interference filter, plus bialkali with 400-500 nm filter; per-band absolute radiometric calibration; sensitivity floor ~1 photon/s/cm2 per band.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: The register's H4a asserts a fraction of intensity explained by ROS chemistry but assigns no reaction order to any band. This converts 'the UV is unexplained' into a single dimensionless number, beta, whose value discriminates single-quantum chemiexcitation (beta=1) from pairwise excitation pooling (beta=2), and derives the 175 nm floor of the pooling channel from the field's own 350 nm carbonyl edge - showing that the historically claimed 190-250 nm window is precisely the interval that pairwise pooling can reach and single-step chemiexcitation cannot.

members.statement: Measured with a solar-blind photocathode and a fully quartz optical train, the absolute spontaneous photon flux below 320 nm from a proliferating cell culture is less than 1% of its 350-700 nm flux, i.e. more than an order of magnitude below the 20-40% UV fraction and the 10-1000 photons/cm2/s mitogenetic level claimed in the historical record.

hypothesis.statement: Measured with a solar-blind photocathode and a fully quartz optical train, the absolute spontaneous photon flux below 320 nm from a proliferating cell culture is less than 1% of its 350-700 nm flux, i.e. more than an order of magnitude below the 20-40% UV fraction and the 10-1000 photons/cm2/s mitogenetic level claimed in the historical record.

scope.population: Exponentially growing Saccharomyces cerevisiae and a proliferating mammalian line (HeLa or A549) in quartz vessels, dark-adapted >2 h, 25-37 C; onion-root or yeast preparations of the classic mitogenetic type included as a positive-control arm
scope.condition: Spontaneous (unstimulated) emission recorded through a CsTe or CsI solar-blind photocathode with out-of-band rejection >1e5 above 350 nm, quartz windows throughout, against a paired 350-700 nm bialkali channel
scope.comparator: Identical acquisition on heat-killed cells, on cell-free medium, and on the same live culture behind a UV-blocking borosilicate window; plus the historically asserted values (20-40% UV fraction; 10-1000 photons/cm2/s at 190-250 nm)
scope.outcome: Absolute background-subtracted photon flux in photons/cm2/s in the <320 nm band, and its ratio to the simultaneously measured 350-700 nm flux

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The <320 nm flux is >=5% of the 350-700 nm flux, or exceeds 10 photons/cm2/s in absolute terms, in live cultures and not in heat-killed or medium controls - which would confirm a large genuine UV component and force a new generating chemistry.
hypothesis.estimand: f_UV = (absolute photons/cm2/s in 190-320 nm) / (absolute photons/cm2/s in 350-700 nm), with a two-sided 95% CI; and the absolute <320 nm flux itself with its detection limit stated.

rationale.step: The historical mitogenetic literature specifies both an intensity (~10-1000 photons/cm2/s) and a band (~190-250 nm), giving a directly testable absolute target rather than a relative one.

A critical review of the same literature concludes there is little modern evidence even for the longer UV interval 280-390 nm, while a separate review concludes the UV fraction should be regarded as real - the two reviews disagree on the same object, which is the definition of an unaudited measurement.

Modern instruments that report UPE over a 200-1000 nm range in fact use EMCCD and CCD cameras described as capturing single visible-wavelength photons, so the sub-350 nm end of the quoted range is asserted by the stated band rather than measured by the stated detector; a hand-UPE spectrometer built on an EMCCD plus tunable filter likewise sampled only 400-700 nm.

The absolute-calibration audit is a proven design in this corpus: photon emission from isolated frog and fish retinas was quantified against a calibrated source and found >=100x too weak to sustain the biophoton hypothesis of photoreceptor dark noise, retiring that claim decisively.

The required sensitivity exists. EMCCD binary photon counting reaches SNR 3 at fluxes below 30 photons/s/cm2, and a high-albedo Ulbricht-cavity concentrator pushes lower still, having detected the luminescence of non-catalytic H2O2 disproportionation in pure water. If the historical 20-40% fraction were real, given total UPE of 10-1000 photons/cm2/s the UV band would carry 2-400 photons/cm2/s, comfortably above these floors; a null at that sensitivity is therefore informative rather than merely underpowered.

Solar-blind photocathodes are the correct instrument class precisely because the failure mode being tested is red leakage: a bialkali cathode peaks near 350-420 nm, so any coloured-glass or interference filter with finite out-of-band transmission converts abundant blue-green carbonyl photons into apparent UV counts. A CsTe cathode with >1e5 rejection above 350 nm removes that pathway physically rather than by subtraction.

Borosilicate optics are common in this literature (a luminometer arm using borosilicate test tubes is used to report 300-400 nm band intensities), so a paired borosilicate-versus-quartz arm is a necessary control on whether reported UV is transmitted at all.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Assemble a solar-blind channel: sample in a fused-silica vessel inside a light-tight, temperature-controlled dark chamber; all-quartz collection; a cooled CsTe (or CsI) PMT in photon counting, with a solar-blind bandpass defining 190-320 nm; and a simultaneous bialkali channel at 350-700 nm through a beam splitter. Calibrate both channels absolutely against a traceable attenuated deuterium/tungsten source so that counts map to photons/cm2/s at the sample surface. Optionally couple the sample into a high-albedo quartz-powder Ulbricht cavity to convert the 3D emitting volume into a small high-radiance orifice and gain roughly two orders of magnitude in effective sensitivity. Acquire >=4 h per condition on: exponential yeast, exponential mammalian culture, onion-root positive control, heat-killed cells, sterile medium, empty vessel, and live culture behind borosilicate. Report f_UV with CIs and state the detection limit explicitly. Pre-register the decision rule: f_UV < 0.01 refutes the 20-40% claim; f_UV >= 0.05 with live-versus-killed separation confirms it.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Cooled solar-blind CsTe/CsI photon-counting PMT (190-320 nm, >1e5 out-of-band rejection) with all-fused-silica optics and NIST-traceable absolute calibration, paired with a cooled bialkali 350-700 nm channel; optional high-albedo Ulbricht-cavity photon concentrator.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: Register entries H1 and H11 both presuppose that a UV band exists at a level worth explaining or decoding; none of them contains the absolute per-band flux measurement that would license the presupposition. This makes the presupposition itself the estimand, sets the pass/fail against numbers the historical literature actually committed to (20-40%; 10-1000 photons/cm2/s at 190-250 nm), and specifies the one detector class - solar-blind photocathode plus all-quartz train - under which a positive result cannot be red leakage. It resolves a live contradiction between two reviews in the corpus rather than adding to it.

members.statement: The externally measured sub-350 nm fraction of UPE is set by aromatic-amino-acid self-absorption inside the sample, so it declines with optical depth according to Beer-Lambert with the tryptophan extinction coefficient, and the same preparation measured at 0.1 mm path emits a UV/visible ratio at least fivefold higher than at 10 mm path, at matched total oxidative flux.

hypothesis.statement: The externally measured sub-350 nm fraction of UPE is set by aromatic-amino-acid self-absorption inside the sample, so it declines with optical depth according to Beer-Lambert with the tryptophan extinction coefficient, and the same preparation measured at 0.1 mm path emits a UV/visible ratio at least fivefold higher than at 10 mm path, at matched total oxidative flux.

scope.population: One cell suspension (yeast or HeLa) and one cell-free protein-plus-lipid oxidation mixture, each measured at four optical depths (0.1, 1, 3, 10 mm quartz path) and three volume fractions spanning 100-fold, with total oxidative turnover held constant per unit emitting volume
scope.condition: Constant chemical trigger (fixed Fe(II)/H2O2 or fixed linoleic-acid dose per unit volume), varying only geometry and packing
scope.comparator: The same series measured in the 450-500 nm band, where aromatic-residue absorption is negligible, which must show no comparable geometry dependence
scope.outcome: Ratio R(d) = flux(280-340 nm)/flux(450-500 nm) as a function of effective optical depth d = (volume fraction x path length)

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: R(d) is flat within 20% across a 100-fold change in effective optical depth, i.e. the escaping UV fraction is geometry-independent, which would mean the measured spectrum is the generated spectrum and self-absorption cannot explain the apparent UV deficit.
hypothesis.estimand: The fitted decay constant of ln R(d) against d, compared with the Beer-Lambert prediction 2.303 x epsilon_Trp x c_Trp; agreement within a factor of 2 supports, a fitted constant consistent with zero refutes.

rationale.step: The field's own reference text states that the reabsorption effect increases with the sample optical density in the luminescing system and is governed by the absorption spectra of substances present - so the mechanism is acknowledged in principle but is not used as a quantitative correction on reported UV fractions.

Tryptophan is not a bystander in this system: on oxidation of amino acids it both emits and acts as an energy acceptor, and mixing histidine with tryptophan yields a spectrum congruent with pure tryptophan, demonstrating that the aromatic pool dominates the sub-350 nm optical behaviour of an oxidising protein sample.

Aromatic residues are also the designated absorbers in this corpus's transport models, with microtubule reorientation to exogenous photons peaking near 280 nm in the tryptophan/tyrosine absorption range - the same band whose emission is reported missing.

Beer-Lambert arithmetic makes the geometry dependence extreme rather than marginal. With epsilon_Trp near 5.5e3 M^-1 cm^-1 at 280 nm and intracellular protein-bound tryptophan of order 3 mM: a single 10 um cell has A = 5.5e3 x 3e-3 x 1e-3 = 0.017, transmission 96%, effectively transparent; a 1 cm path of packed cells has A = 16.5, transmission ~3e-17, effectively opaque; a 1 cm path of a 0.2% v/v suspension has A = 0.033, transmission 93%. The escaping UV fraction therefore varies over sixteen orders of magnitude across preparations that the literature reports side by side, while the 450-500 nm band, where epsilon is near zero, varies not at all.

The corpus supplies direct evidence that the in-vivo spectrum is not the in-vitro spectrum: in-vitro lipid oxidation luminesces across 450-850 nm, whereas the in-planta signal from leaves and roots occurs only above 640 nm, peaking at 700-750 nm. Something in the tissue removes the short-wave half of the generated spectrum.

A scattering/geometry treatment of stress-induced emission and a photon-diffusion treatment of human surface emission both already exist in this corpus, so the modelling machinery for converting surface flux to source flux is available and can be fitted rather than assumed.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Use demountable fused-silica cells at 0.1, 1, 3 and 10 mm path with identical face area, so emitting area is constant and only depth varies. For each of three volume fractions, trigger a fixed per-volume oxidative dose and record simultaneously through 280-340 nm and 450-500 nm interference filters, either by dual PMT or by an EMCCD in binary photon-counting mode behind a tunable filter, absolutely calibrated per band. Independently measure the sample's own absorbance spectrum at each condition on a standard spectrophotometer so epsilon x c is measured, not assumed, and quantify total tryptophan by amino-acid analysis. Fit ln R(d) against measured absorbance-derived d. Run the whole matrix a second time after exhaustive proteolysis plus dialysis to strip aromatic residues at constant lipid load: the predicted result is that R becomes flat with depth in the stripped arm. A flat R(d) in the intact arm refutes the hypothesis outright.
hypothesis.required_instrument: EMCCD in binary photon-counting mode (or dual cooled PMT) with 280-340 nm and 450-500 nm interference filters and quartz optics; variable-path demountable fused-silica cells; a companion UV-Vis spectrophotometer for per-sample absorbance.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: Every claim on the register that reads a spectrum - H4a's accounting of intensity, H11's spectral information content, H1's UV band, H2's optical state - silently assumes the escaping spectrum equals the generated spectrum. This names that assumption, shows by Beer-Lambert arithmetic that it fails by up to sixteen orders of magnitude in the UV specifically and not at all in the blue-green, and turns it into a single fitted decay constant measurable in an afternoon with a variable-path cell. If it holds, the UV is not missing but trapped, and 'unexplained UV' is a transport result misfiled as a generation result.

members.statement: Under strict anoxia (<10 ppm O2) the sub-350 nm and the 450-550 nm bands of wound-induced and chemically induced UPE are suppressed by the same factor within 25%, i.e. the UV band has no oxygen-independent component and therefore no source outside the catalogued ROS chemistry.

hypothesis.statement: Under strict anoxia (<10 ppm O2) the sub-350 nm and the 450-550 nm bands of wound-induced and chemically induced UPE are suppressed by the same factor within 25%, i.e. the UV band has no oxygen-independent component and therefore no source outside the catalogued ROS chemistry.

scope.population: Detached Spathiphyllum or Arabidopsis leaves subjected to standardised mechanical wounding, plus a yeast culture subjected to a fixed H2O2 challenge, in a sealed quartz chamber with an in-line O2 sensor
scope.condition: Three atmospheres: air (21% O2), 2% O2, and strict anoxia (<10 ppm O2, N2-purged with getter), wound or challenge applied inside the chamber after 2 h dark adaptation
scope.comparator: The air arm of the same preparation, and the paired 450-550 nm band measured simultaneously
scope.outcome: Suppression ratio S_band = flux(anoxia)/flux(air) computed separately for 260-340 nm and 450-550 nm; the contrast of interest is S_UV / S_vis

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: S_UV / S_vis exceeds 1.25 with a 95% CI excluding 1.0 - i.e. a residual UV emission survives anoxia that the visible band does not - which would demonstrate an oxygen-independent UV source and falsify the claim that the catalogued ROS chemistry exhausts the UV band.
hypothesis.estimand: S_UV / S_vis with a 95% CI; equivalence within [0.8, 1.25] supports, exclusion of 1.0 refutes.

rationale.step: Oxygen dependence is already an established, reproducible handle on this system: wound-induced leaf UPE is significantly suppressed under anoxic stress while pre-wound basal photocounts are unaffected by nitrogen incubation, so the experimental arm and its own internal control both exist.

The catalogued mechanism makes oxygen dependence obligatory for every product: ROS oxidation of lipids, proteins and nucleic acids forms dioxetane and tetroxide intermediates whose decomposition yields triplet carbonyls, and singlet oxygen arises by triplet-singlet transfer from those carbonyls to ground-state O2 - so both the primary and the secondary emitters vanish together when O2 is removed.

Anoxia is therefore a single knob that acts on the whole catalogued pathway at once, which makes band-resolved anoxia a clean discriminator: a shared suppression factor localises the UV inside the pathway, whereas any surviving UV localises a source outside it.

Candidate oxygen-independent UV sources are present in the corpus and would be the beneficiaries of a positive result: mechanically induced long-lived luminescence in shaken aqueous solutions, triboluminescence as a biological phenomenon, and free-radical recombination reactions in water systems tabulated with their enthalpies.

The wounding preparation additionally has independent ROS readouts - superoxide and singlet oxygen imaged directly in wounded Arabidopsis leaves - so the O2 titration can be verified chemically rather than inferred from the light alone.

The measurement must be band-resolved and simultaneous, because the wound response is kinetically structured: aerobic wounding induces two distinct exponential decay events, so sequential single-band acquisition would confound band with time.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Mount the leaf or culture in a sealed fused-silica chamber with feedthroughs for a remote-actuated wounding blade and an in-line trace-O2 sensor reading to <10 ppm; purge with N2 through an oxygen getter. Collect through a quartz train split by a 380 nm dichroic onto two cooled photon counters, 260-340 nm (UV-extended or CsTe cathode) and 450-550 nm (bialkali), both absolutely calibrated. Protocol per replicate: 2 h dark adapt, 30 min baseline, wound (or inject H2O2), record 60 min, in each of the three atmospheres, with the atmosphere order randomised across replicates and >=8 biological replicates per arm. Confirm the ROS titration independently by fluorescent superoxide and singlet-oxygen imaging on sibling samples. Compute S_UV and S_vis from time-integrated absolute fluxes and test S_UV/S_vis for equivalence in [0.8, 1.25]. Include a leakage control in which the UV filter is replaced by a blocked equivalent at every atmosphere, so any anoxia-surviving UV must exceed leakage.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Sealed quartz anoxia chamber with <10 ppm O2 sensing, feeding a dual-channel cooled photon-counting PMT bench at 260-340 nm (UV-extended bialkali or CsTe) and 450-550 nm (bialkali), absolutely calibrated per band.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: H4a claims the ROS pathway carries the dominant fraction of intensity but is stated over total intensity and offers no way to fail band-by-band. This makes anoxia a per-band test with a pre-set equivalence interval, so a surviving sub-350 nm component under strict anoxia would carve a specific, bounded exception out of H4a rather than merely qualifying it - and would nominate named oxygen-independent candidates already in the corpus (mechanoluminescence, triboluminescence, aqueous radical recombination) as the residual source.

members.statement: Deuteration of the solvent enhances the sub-350 nm UPE band by the same factor as it enhances the 620-720 nm singlet-oxygen dimol band, establishing that the sub-350 nm emission lies downstream of singlet oxygen rather than arising directly from triplet carbonyls, whose lifetime is deuteration-insensitive.

In H2O2-stressed U266 multiple-myeloma cells, perturbations that lengthen or quench singlet-oxygen lifetime will change 300–349 nm photon flux in the same direction as 1,270 nm singlet-oxygen emission and more strongly than 340–540 nm triplet-carbonyl emission.

hypothesis.statement: Deuteration of the solvent enhances the sub-350 nm UPE band by the same factor as it enhances the 620-720 nm singlet-oxygen dimol band, establishing that the sub-350 nm emission lies downstream of singlet oxygen rather than arising directly from triplet carbonyls, whose lifetime is deuteration-insensitive.

scope.population: Rat or porcine skin homogenate and a defined lipid-plus-tryptophan cell-free oxidation mixture, each prepared in matched H2O and D2O buffers of identical ionic strength and pH/pD
scope.condition: Fixed oxidative trigger (UV irradiation of the homogenate, or Fe(II)/H2O2 of the defined mixture), measured in four bands simultaneously or in rapid rotation: 260-340 nm, 400-500 nm, 620-720 nm, and 1270 nm
scope.comparator: The matched H2O preparation; and the DABCO-quenched and azide-quenched arms of both solvents
scope.outcome: Per-band deuteration enhancement E_band = flux(D2O)/flux(H2O), and the contrast rho = E_UV / E_dimol

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: rho is significantly below 1 (e.g. E_dimol near 3 while E_UV is near 1), i.e. the UV band is deuteration-insensitive while the red dimol band is strongly enhanced - which excludes singlet oxygen as the UV precursor and points instead to a direct carbonyl-pooling or aromatic-residue route.
hypothesis.estimand: rho = E_UV / E_dimol with a 95% CI; rho within [0.7, 1.4] supports a singlet-oxygen-downstream UV, rho < 0.5 refutes it.

rationale.step: Solvent deuteration is an established, quantified perturbation for this exact class of signal in this corpus: substituting D2O for H2O enhanced ultraweak chemiluminescence of rat epidermal homogenate to 300%, while the singlet-oxygen quencher DABCO reduced it to 50%.

The red band it should act on is spectrally identified: singlet oxygen dimol emission has bands at 634 and 703 nm with a characteristic low point near 668 nm, and DABCO's action on monomol (1270 nm) versus dimol emission has been characterised - though its enhancement is not universal, so azide quenching must be run as an independent check rather than relying on DABCO alone.

The mechanistic asymmetry that makes this a discriminator: deuteration lengthens the singlet-oxygen lifetime and therefore raises the yield of every channel fed by singlet oxygen, while triplet carbonyl lifetimes are not governed by solvent O-H/O-D coupling. Bands sharing a factor therefore share a precursor; bands whose factors diverge do not.

A concrete singlet-oxygen-to-UV route exists in the corpus: singlet oxygen oxidises tryptophan to isomeric hydroperoxides whose decomposition to N-formylkynurenine is chemiluminescent, and tryptophan is the dominant energy acceptor in oxidised protein samples - giving singlet oxygen a specific chemical path into the aromatic emitter that occupies the sub-350 nm region.

The counter-route is equally concrete: excited carbonyls generate singlet oxygen by triplet-triplet energy transfer to ground-state O2, so causality runs carbonyl-to-singlet-oxygen in the established scheme. If the UV instead tracked the carbonyl band and not the dimol band, the UV would sit upstream of singlet oxygen, inverting the assumed order.

Skin homogenate is the right matrix because a minimal chemical model of skin built from lipid, melanin and water already reproduces essential features of real skin's autoluminescence response, so a cell-free arm and a tissue arm can be compared without changing the chemistry.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Prepare matched H2O and D2O buffers (>=99% D, pD corrected) and split each homogenate or defined mixture between them. Apply the fixed trigger and acquire four bands: 260-340 nm and 400-500 nm on cooled UV-capable and bialkali PMTs through quartz, 620-720 nm on a red-sensitive PMT with the 634/668/703 nm three-point sampling that identifies dimol emission, and 1270 nm on a cooled Ge or InGaAs detector for monomol confirmation. Absolutely calibrate each band. Compute E_band for each of the four bands and form rho. Run azide and DABCO quench arms in both solvents at matched concentration to confirm that the red band responds as singlet oxygen and to test whether the UV band inherits the same quench sensitivity. Pre-register: rho in [0.7, 1.4] with E_dimol significantly >1 supports; rho < 0.5 refutes and reassigns the UV upstream of singlet oxygen.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Four-band photon-counting bench: cooled UV-extended PMT with quartz optics for 260-340 nm, bialkali for 400-500 nm, red-extended (multialkali/GaAs) PMT for 620-720 nm, and cooled Ge or InGaAs detector for 1270 nm; per-band absolute calibration.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: The field's own prescription is targeted chemical perturbation of candidate ROS pathways extended below 350 nm, but the register contains no claim that ties a specific perturbation to a specific band ratio. This turns solvent deuteration - already quantified at 300% for total skin chemiluminescence in this corpus - into a per-band contrast rho whose value fixes whether the UV band sits upstream or downstream of singlet oxygen, using an isotope substitution that changes no concentration, no dose and no geometry.

members.statement: The spectral shape of UPE, including the size of its sub-350 nm fraction, is set by the acceptor-chromophore inventory of the preparation rather than by the primary chemiexcitation step, such that adding melanin or chlorophyll at fixed oxidative chemistry suppresses the sub-350 nm fraction by more than half while leaving total emitted photon number changed by less than 30%.

After linoleic-acid challenge of dark-adapted Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, a chlorophyll-deficient line will retain a 300–349 nm transient at matched lipid-peroxidation burden while losing the 680 nm peak, revealing primary oxidative excitation that is normally transferred to chlorophyll.

hypothesis.statement: The spectral shape of UPE, including the size of its sub-350 nm fraction, is set by the acceptor-chromophore inventory of the preparation rather than by the primary chemiexcitation step, such that adding melanin or chlorophyll at fixed oxidative chemistry suppresses the sub-350 nm fraction by more than half while leaving total emitted photon number changed by less than 30%.

scope.population: A minimal cell-free skin-model oxidation system (lipid + water) run at fixed Fe(II)/H2O2 or fixed UVA dose, with a titrated acceptor added: synthetic melanin, chlorophyll a, or bovine serum albumin as a tryptophan-bearing acceptor, at four concentrations spanning 100-fold
scope.condition: Identical primary chemistry across all arms, verified by matched malondialdehyde/peroxide-value assay, with only the added acceptor varying
scope.comparator: The acceptor-free arm of the same chemistry; and, as a cross-check, the same chemistry run in a matrix that already contains a dominant acceptor (leaf tissue, pigmented skin)
scope.outcome: Fraction of total emitted photons in 260-340 nm, and total emitted photons integrated 260-900 nm, as functions of acceptor concentration

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The sub-350 nm fraction is invariant to acceptor concentration (change <20% across a 100-fold acceptor titration) at matched oxidative turnover, i.e. the emitted spectrum is a property of the primary chemistry and acceptors merely attenuate everything proportionally.
hypothesis.estimand: The ratio (sub-350 nm fraction at highest acceptor)/(sub-350 nm fraction at zero acceptor), with total-photon conservation reported alongside; <0.5 with total photons within 30% supports, >0.8 refutes.

rationale.step: Energy transfer from the primary excited species to a secondary chromophore is the corpus's own stated mechanism: when chromophores are proximate to triplet excited carbonyls, triplet-singlet and triplet-triplet transfer produce excited chromophores, so the emitting species need not be the excited species.

The acceptor is demonstrably able to overwrite the spectrum. Histidine and tryptophan give strikingly different individual UPE spectra of comparable strength, yet their mixture yields a spectrum congruent with pure tryptophan - the acceptor's spectrum, not a sum of the generators'.

The same overwrite is documented across matrices. In vitro lipid oxidation luminesces across 450-850 nm, but the in-planta signal appears only above 640 nm, peaking at 700-750 nm; wound emission from two plant species is reported above 650 nm with chlorophyll named as the likely emitter; and in skin, triplet carbonyls transfer their excitation to melanin by either radiative or electron-exchange routes, forming melanin-based secondary excited states.

Melanin chemiexcitation is established beyond UPE work: chemically generated triplet states on melanin fragments carry the energy of a UV photon and transfer it to DNA to produce cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers hours after irradiation ends, and the same mechanism is invoked for retinal melanin. So melanin is a competent, well-characterised acceptor operating at exactly the energies in dispute.

The energy bookkeeping predicts the asymmetry that makes this testable. Acceptor capture is a downhill transfer, so it moves quanta from short to long wavelength while approximately conserving photon number; a pure inner-filter loss would instead destroy photons. Measuring the sub-350 nm fraction and the total integrated photon count together therefore separates spectral redistribution from attenuation, and only redistribution supports the claim.

The minimal chemical model needed already exists in this corpus: a lipid-melanin-water mixture reproduces essential features of real skin's autoluminescence response to oxidative stress, so acceptor titration can be done at genuinely fixed chemistry.

If confirmed, the corollary is that the sub-350 nm band is not weak because it is rarely generated but because almost every biological matrix is acceptor-rich - which reframes the seed question and predicts the largest UV fractions in the most acceptor-poor preparations (aliphatic lipid systems, albino or amelanotic tissue) rather than in the most metabolically active ones.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Run the lipid-plus-water minimal skin model at a single fixed oxidative trigger, in fused-silica cuvettes, with four titrated levels each of synthetic melanin, chlorophyll a, and BSA, plus an acceptor-free arm. At every arm, acquire the full 260-900 nm emission with an imaging spectrograph coupled to a cooled EMCCD in binary photon-counting mode, absolutely calibrated for spectral response so photon numbers, not counts, are compared; supplement below 350 nm with a solar-blind PMT channel where spectrograph throughput is marginal. Hold the primary chemistry constant and prove it: measure peroxide value and HPLC malondialdehyde in every arm and reject any arm whose turnover deviates by more than 15%. Measure each acceptor's own absorbance spectrum in situ so that a pure inner-filter prediction can be computed and subtracted, isolating genuine transfer-driven redistribution. Cross-check in tissue by comparing amelanotic and pigmented skin, and chlorophyll-containing versus etiolated plant tissue, at matched wounding. Decision: sub-350 nm fraction falling by >50% while total 260-900 nm photons stay within 30% supports; either invariance of the fraction, or proportional loss of total photons, refutes.
hypothesis.required_instrument: UV-Vis imaging spectrograph (250-900 nm, quartz/fused-silica throughout) coupled to a cooled EMCCD in binary photon-counting mode with absolute spectral-response calibration, plus a solar-blind PMT channel for the 260-340 nm sub-band; companion UV-Vis spectrophotometer for in-situ acceptor absorbance.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: H11 holds that the UPE spectral distribution carries state-specific information beyond total intensity. This proposes the rival that would have to be excluded first: the spectrum is a readout of the acceptor-chromophore inventory, so a spectral shift can be produced by pigment content at completely fixed oxidative chemistry. It also converts the seed's rival mechanisms - primary carbonyl emission versus melanin secondary emission from the porcine-skin work - into a titration with a numeric decision rule, and separates spectral redistribution from inner-filter attenuation by requiring total photon number to be conserved, a control the acceptor literature in this corpus does not report.

members.statement: In Fe2+/H2O2-oxidized recombinant human serum albumin, replacing its tryptophan with phenylalanine will selectively reduce calibrated 250–349 nm emission relative to 350–550 nm emission at matched protein-carbonyl burden, identifying tryptophan as a final UV emitter receiving chemiexcitation energy.

hypothesis.statement: In Fe2+/H2O2-oxidized recombinant human serum albumin, replacing its tryptophan with phenylalanine will selectively reduce calibrated 250–349 nm emission relative to 350–550 nm emission at matched protein-carbonyl burden, identifying tryptophan as a final UV emitter receiving chemiexcitation energy.

scope.population: Purified recombinant wild-type human serum albumin and an otherwise matched Trp-to-Phe variant in quartz cuvettes.
scope.condition: Dark Fe2+/H2O2 oxidation at matched temperature, dissolved oxygen, protein concentration and measured carbonyl burden.
scope.comparator: Wild-type versus Trp-to-Phe albumin, with unoxidized and fluorophore-free reaction blanks.
scope.outcome: Absolute photon flux in 250–299, 300–349 and 350–550 nm bands, plus protein-carbonyl concentration.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The Trp-to-Phe substitution does not lower the 250–349/350–550 nm photon-flux ratio; a 95% confidence interval for the contrast includes or lies below zero.
hypothesis.estimand: θ=ln[(F250–349/F350–550)WT/(F250–349/F350–550)Trp→Phe] at equal carbonyl burden; the claim requires θ>0.

rationale.step: The origin of biological UPE below 350 nm is explicitly unresolved.
Oxidized protein and amino-acid systems emit UPE, and tryptophan can receive excitation energy from other oxidized amino acids and act as the final emitter.
ROS oxidation can form triplet carbonyls whose energy is transferred to nearby chromophores.
Taking the ratio of UV to visible flux before comparing genotypes separates a band-specific emitter effect from a uniform change in reaction yield.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Oxidize wild-type and Trp-to-Phe albumin in randomized replicate quartz cuvettes, continuously measure calibrated band-resolved photons, and quantify carbonyls by an orthogonal assay; fit photon flux against carbonyl burden and test the genotype-by-band interaction.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Light-tight integrating collection chamber with quartz optics, an absolutely calibrated photon-counting UV spectrograph or parallel UV-enhanced PMTs covering 250–550 nm, and 10–25 nm bandpass filters.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This converts the broad ROS-origin claim into a residue-level causal test of the unidentified sub-350 nm final emitter.

members.statement: In genetically plasmalogen-deficient human keratinocytes, restoring plasmalogens will increase dark post-oxidation 300–349 nm flux at a fixed singlet-oxygen dose and lipid-peroxide burden, with the increase scaling with hydroperoxyacetal and dioxetane products.

hypothesis.statement: In genetically plasmalogen-deficient human keratinocytes, restoring plasmalogens will increase dark post-oxidation 300–349 nm flux at a fixed singlet-oxygen dose and lipid-peroxide burden, with the increase scaling with hydroperoxyacetal and dioxetane products.

scope.population: Isogenic plasmalogen-deficient and genetically rescued human keratinocyte cultures, with lipidomics-confirmed plasmalogen abundance.
scope.condition: A matched pulse from a dark singlet-oxygen donor followed by photon recording after donor-only background subtraction.
scope.comparator: Deficient versus rescued cells, plus untreated cells and donor-only medium.
scope.outcome: Absolute 300–349, 350–550 and 1,270 nm photon fluxes and LC-HRMS abundances of plasmalogen hydroperoxyacetals, dioxetanes and lipid peroxides.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: Plasmalogen rescue does not increase 300–349 nm flux after adjustment for delivered singlet oxygen, cell number and total lipid-peroxide burden, and UV flux does not covary with the specified plasmalogen products.
hypothesis.estimand: θ=ln(F300–349,rescued/F300–349,deficient) standardized to equal singlet-oxygen exposure and total lipid peroxide; the claim requires θ>0 and a positive product–flux slope.

rationale.step: Plasmalogen oxidation forms hydroperoxyacetal and dioxetane intermediates that subsequently generate triplet carbonyls and singlet oxygen, demonstrated by visible and 1,270 nm emission and LC-HRMS.
Dioxetane and tetroxide decomposition are candidate sources of triplet carbonyls, which can emit or transfer energy to cellular chromophores.
Normalizing the rescue contrast to singlet-oxygen dose and total lipid-peroxide burden isolates the plasmalogen branch from a nonspecific increase in oxidation.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Verify plasmalogen depletion and rescue by lipidomics, expose equal cell numbers to a calibrated dark singlet-oxygen pulse, record emission continuously in three bands, and use LC-HRMS time points to test whether plasmalogen intermediates mediate the rescued UV signal.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Absolutely calibrated UV-visible photon-counting spectrograph with quartz optics covering 300–550 nm, a cooled 1,270 nm single-photon detector and LC-HRMS.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This tests a newly demonstrated lipid branch as a specific source of the unresolved UV band rather than treating all lipid peroxidation as one mechanism.

members.statement: In UVA-exposed ex vivo porcine skin, trapping formaldehyde and acetaldehyde immediately after irradiation will suppress 300–349 nm afterglow more than 1,270 nm emission while leaving the initiating radical burden substantially intact, identifying short-chain triplet carbonyls as proximal UV emitters.

hypothesis.statement: In UVA-exposed ex vivo porcine skin, trapping formaldehyde and acetaldehyde immediately after irradiation will suppress 300–349 nm afterglow more than 1,270 nm emission while leaving the initiating radical burden substantially intact, identifying short-chain triplet carbonyls as proximal UV emitters.

scope.population: Adjacent, randomized ex vivo porcine-skin biopsies from the same animals.
scope.condition: Standardized UVA exposure followed by dark recording with vehicle or each of two chemically distinct carbonyl traps.
scope.comparator: Vehicle, carbonyl-trap, singlet-oxygen-quencher, sham-irradiated and reagent-only biopsies.
scope.outcome: Absolute post-UVA photon flux in 300–349, 350–500 and 1,270±10 nm bands; free formaldehyde/acetaldehyde by LC-MS; organic radicals by EPR.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: Carbonyl trapping does not preferentially reduce 300–349 nm flux relative to 1,270 nm flux, or any reduction is fully explained by loss of the initiating radical signal.
hypothesis.estimand: θ=[1−FUV,trap/FUV,vehicle]−[1−F1270,trap/F1270,vehicle]; the claim requires θ>0 after adjustment for EPR radical burden.

rationale.step: UVA-exposed porcine skin forms lipid-derived radicals and short-chain carbonyls, particularly formaldehyde and acetaldehyde, with triplet-carbonyl excitation and possible energy transfer to melanin after irradiation ends.
Oxidative-radical reactions in porcine skin produce measurable 340–540 nm triplet-carbonyl emission and singlet-oxygen contributions in the visible and near-infrared.
Subtracting fractional inhibition at 1,270 nm from fractional UV inhibition distinguishes direct carbonyl-band loss from generalized suppression of singlet-oxygen chemistry.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Treat matched biopsies with vehicle or two carbonyl traps, apply identical UVA doses, begin photon acquisition immediately after shutter closure, and jointly model band-resolved decay, LC-MS carbonyl depletion and EPR radical persistence.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Shutter-synchronized, absolutely calibrated UV-visible photon-counting spectrograph covering 280–550 nm, cooled 1,270 nm single-photon detector, EPR spin-trapping system and LC-MS.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This extends the porcine-skin chemiexcitation program below 350 nm and separates short-chain carbonyl emission from singlet-oxygen emission.

members.statement: In dark-adapted permeabilized human keratinocytes supplied with defined respiratory substrates, rotenone-induced mitochondrial electron leak will selectively raise 300–349 nm flux, and a mitochondria-targeted antioxidant will abolish that increment more strongly than the 650–750 nm increment.

hypothesis.statement: In dark-adapted permeabilized human keratinocytes supplied with defined respiratory substrates, rotenone-induced mitochondrial electron leak will selectively raise 300–349 nm flux, and a mitochondria-targeted antioxidant will abolish that increment more strongly than the 650–750 nm increment.

scope.population: Permeabilized, viable HaCaT human keratinocytes with intact mitochondria.
scope.condition: Defined complex-I-linked respiratory substrate with vehicle, rotenone, mitochondria-targeted antioxidant, or their combination under controlled oxygen tension.
scope.comparator: Vehicle respiration, rotenone alone, antioxidant alone and mitochondria-depleted lysate controls.
scope.outcome: Absolute 300–349, 350–550 and 650–750 nm photon flux, mitochondrial H2O2 production, oxygen-consumption rate and viability.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: Rotenone produces no 300–349 nm increment, or the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant does not suppress that increment more than the 650–750 nm increment.
hypothesis.estimand: θ={ln(FUV,rotenone/FUV,vehicle)−ln(FUV,rotenone+antioxidant/FUV,antioxidant)}−{the analogous 650–750 nm contrast}; the claim requires θ>0.

rationale.step: Mitochondria are proposed to produce a major fraction of cellular UPE through respiration-related ROS formation.
Rotenone increased spontaneous photon emission from rat brain, consistent with electron leakage from the respiratory chain.
ROS oxidation of lipids, proteins and nucleic acids can converge on triplet-carbonyl, excited-chromophore and singlet-oxygen production.
The difference between antioxidant-sensitive rotenone effects in UV and red bands is a band-specific mitochondrial-source interaction rather than a total-intensity test.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Measure simultaneous respiration, mitochondrial H2O2 and calibrated spectral flux during sequential substrate, rotenone and antioxidant additions; repeat in mitochondria-depleted lysate and fit the prespecified band-by-treatment interaction.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Quartz-window respirometry chamber coupled to an absolutely calibrated UV-visible photon-counting spectrograph spanning 300–750 nm, plus a fluorometric or electrochemical mitochondrial H2O2 assay.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This localizes the unresolved UV component to—or excludes it from—respiratory-chain electron leak while separating it from red lipid/chromophore emission.

members.statement: The photon degeneracy parameter delta (mean photon occupation per electromagnetic mode, delta = L_nu * lambda^2) of spontaneous UPE is below 1e-15 in every biological preparation, which places the Hanbury-Brown-Twiss bunching excess of any photocount experiment more than ten orders of magnitude below its own shot noise, so no photocount statistic measured on spontaneous UPE can discriminate a coherent from a chaotic field at any achievable integration time.

hypothesis.statement: The photon degeneracy parameter delta (mean photon occupation per electromagnetic mode, delta = L_nu * lambda^2) of spontaneous UPE is below 1e-15 in every biological preparation, which places the Hanbury-Brown-Twiss bunching excess of any photocount experiment more than ten orders of magnitude below its own shot noise, so no photocount statistic measured on spontaneous UPE can discriminate a coherent from a chaotic field at any achievable integration time.

scope.population: Three standard preparations measured under one calibration: germinating Vigna radiata (mung bean) beds, log-phase aerobic Saccharomyces cerevisiae cultures, and dark-adapted human dorsal hand skin.
scope.condition: Spontaneous (unstimulated) emission in a temperature-clamped (+/-0.05 C) light-tight chamber, absolute spectral radiance measured in 0.1 nm resolution elements across 350-900 nm with a traceably calibrated optical train of known etendue.
scope.comparator: A traceable low-flux transfer standard (attenuated LED / radioluminescent source, calibrated to <5% at ~1e-16 W) measured through the identical optical train and etendue, plus the matched dark run.
scope.outcome: Absolute spectral photon radiance L_nu (photons s-1 cm-2 sr-1 Hz-1), the derived degeneracy delta = L_nu * lambda^2, and the HBT integration time tau = 36/(delta^2 * Delta_nu) implied for SNR = 3.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: Some preparation yields delta >= 1e-15 in at least one 0.1 nm resolution element between 350 and 900 nm, or a mode-counted intensity-correlation measurement on that preparation returns g2(0)-1 significantly larger than 1/M for the independently measured mode number M. Either result kills the claim and re-opens the photocount route.
hypothesis.estimand: delta = L_nu * lambda^2, dimensionless photons per mode, with 95% CI, reported per 0.1 nm resolution element and as the band maximum; secondary estimand is the implied SNR=3 integration time tau.

rationale.step: The field's own critical review states that claims about UPE statistical properties are very controversial and closes by hoping that detectors closer to ideal may bring at least partial answers; a separate UPE review states outright that photocount statistics cannot discriminate a coherent from a thermal state when many modes are collected.

Measured spontaneous UPE flux is a few to some hundred photons per second per square centimetre of surface (10-1e3 photons cm-2 s-1 over 200-1000 nm in recent EMCCD imaging), and a whole cell-culture dish gives roughly 12 photons per second; the emission goes into approximately 2*pi sr over a 350-900 nm continuum.

Compute delta for the optimistic case. Take 1e3 photons s-1 cm-2 into 2*pi sr, lambda = 600 nm, Delta_lambda = 400 nm. Optical bandwidth Delta_nu = c*Delta_lambda/lambda^2 = (3e10 cm/s)(4e-5 cm)/(3.6e-9 cm^2) = 3.3e14 Hz. Photon radiance L = 1e3/(2*pi) = 1.6e2 photons s-1 cm-2 sr-1. Spectral photon radiance L_nu = 1.6e2/3.3e14 = 4.8e-13 photons s-1 cm-2 sr-1 Hz-1. Single-mode etendue = lambda^2 = 3.6e-9 cm^2 sr. Therefore delta = L_nu * lambda^2 = 1.7e-21 photons per mode.

Compute the resulting HBT sensitivity. For chaotic light with M detected modes the fractional bunching excess is g2(0)-1 = 1/M and the excess-to-noise after time tau, at bin T, is SNR = sqrt(R1*R2*T*tau)*(g2(0)-1). Substituting R = delta*Delta_nu*M_spatial and T = 1/Delta_nu (ideal single-temporal-mode timing) gives the mode-independent result SNR = (delta/2)*sqrt(Delta_nu*tau). Setting SNR = 3 with delta = 1.7e-21 and Delta_nu = 3.3e14 Hz gives tau = 36/(delta^2*Delta_nu) = 4e28 s, roughly 1e11 times the age of the universe. Because M_spatial cancels, narrowband filtering, single-mode-fibre selection and light concentration are exactly SNR-neutral: no optical arrangement rescues the measurement.

The corpus contains both signs of this geometry dependence stated qualitatively rather than computed: hand UPE was reported to lack the usual coherence because of the large area and the long measurement time, while 20000-bin photocount fits yielding squeezed parameters were performed in exactly the same many-mode regime with a broadband 300-800 nm detector.

Theory in the corpus establishes that stationary light built from randomly timed emissions acquires the correlation properties of chaotic light in the strong-overlap limit regardless of the statistics of the individual emitters, so the chaotic-light SNR formula above is the correct upper bound for any UPE source model, coherent sub-emitters included.

A field in a genuinely coherent state in the sense claimed by the coherence literature is a macroscopically occupied mode, i.e. delta >= 1. Measuring delta by absolute radiometry therefore tests the coherence claim with a first-order (intensity, etendue, bandwidth) measurement whose sensitivity scales as sqrt(N) rather than as delta, making it ~1e20 times more sensitive than any g2 route; existing calibrated photon-counting radiometry, where detector noise already dominates source photon noise, is adequate to do it.

Light-concentration schemes that raise collected flux (high-albedo integrating cavity with 50% number efficiency) do so by scrambling angle and therefore raise M in exact proportion, confirming operationally that flux gain cannot buy bunching contrast.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Run one traceable radiometric campaign, not a statistics campaign. Calibrate the whole optical train (aperture, solid angle, filter transmission, detector QE, dead time) against a transfer standard traceable to a national metrology institute at the 1e-16 W level. For each of the three preparations, record absolute spectral photon radiance in 0.1 nm resolution elements across 350-900 nm using a grating spectrograph fed to a >90% QE back-illuminated EMCCD photon counter, with interleaved dark and standard-source runs. Report delta = L_nu*lambda^2 per resolution element with uncertainty budget. Then, as a confirmatory arm, run a two-channel HBT on the brightest preparation with the mode number M independently fixed by a single-mode fibre plus a 0.1 nm filter, measure g2(0)-1 and check it against the 1/M prediction and against the delta-derived SNR bound. Pre-register the 1e-15 threshold and the equivalence test.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Traceably calibrated cooled bialkali/multialkali PMT (300-850 nm, <10 dark counts/s) and back-illuminated EMCCD photon-counting array (QE > 90%, 400-900 nm) behind a 0.1 nm-resolution grating spectrograph; low-flux transfer standard calibrated to <5% at ~1e-16 W; two SPAD/SNSPD channels with sub-ns time tagging for the confirmatory HBT arm.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: H2, H2.g2 and H2.sq all presuppose that some photocount statistic could in principle decide coherence. This supplies the single number that decides whether that presupposition is even admissible - the photon degeneracy delta - shows by an auditable calculation that mode selection is SNR-neutral so the photocount route is closed by physics rather than by technique, and replaces it with an absolute-radiometry measurement carrying an explicit falsification threshold (delta >= 1e-15) that appears nowhere in the register.

members.statement: The UPE spectrum of a defined preparation contains no feature narrower than 1 nm anywhere in 400-900 nm, i.e. no emission component with coherence time above ~1.2 ps or coherence length above ~0.36 mm, so first-order (field) coherence of UPE is bounded far below any macroscopic scale.

hypothesis.statement: The UPE spectrum of a defined preparation contains no feature narrower than 1 nm anywhere in 400-900 nm, i.e. no emission component with coherence time above ~1.2 ps or coherence length above ~0.36 mm, so first-order (field) coherence of UPE is bounded far below any macroscopic scale.

scope.population: Mechanically wounded Arabidopsis thaliana leaves (bright, reproducible induced emission with a documented 700-750 nm maximum) and germinating Vigna radiata beds.
scope.condition: Photon-counting Fourier-transform (Michelson) interferometry with optical path difference scanned 0-10 mm under the Jacquinot etendue limit, or equivalently a scanning Fabry-Perot etalon at 0.05 nm resolution, over 400-900 nm; total accumulation 1e5-1e6 s.
scope.comparator: A spectrally flat calibrated continuum source attenuated to the same count rate (negative control) and the same source with a diode-laser line injected at a known 0.3%, 1% and 3% of band flux (positive controls establishing the visibility floor).
scope.outcome: Fringe-visibility envelope |V|(OPD) and the derived maximum line-to-continuum spectral contrast C at 0.1 nm resolution.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: Any preparation shows a visibility revival above the positive-control floor at OPD > 0.5 mm, or a line-to-continuum contrast C > 1.2 in any 0.1 nm resolution element at the pre-registered false-positive rate. That establishes a long-coherence component and falsifies the claim.
hypothesis.estimand: Maximum line-to-continuum spectral contrast C = L_nu(peak)/L_nu(local continuum) at 0.1 nm resolution across 400-900 nm, and the OPD at which |V| first falls below the positive-control floor.

rationale.step: The coherence claim under debate is explicitly a claim about the state of the field: that delayed luminescence and steady-state UPE exhibit mode coupling over the entire spectrum and originate from fully coherent and sometimes squeezed states. A claim about phase coherence is a first-order claim, but the field has only ever tested it with second-order (intensity) statistics.

Compute the sensitivity asymmetry between the two routes. Fringe visibility is estimated from the detected intensity, so its shot-noise error is sigma_V ~ N^-1/2 on N total detected photons, whereas the intensity-correlation route's SNR scales as delta (see Q2-1). At 1e2-1e3 counts s-1 and 1e5 s, N = 1e7-1e8 and sigma_V = 1e-4 to 3e-4 before etendue restriction. Applying the Jacquinot limit Omega <= 2*pi/R with R = lambda/dlambda = 6000 costs roughly 1e-4 of the flux, leaving sigma_V ~ 1e-2 after one day and ~3e-3 after ten days. The required-time ratio between the first-order and second-order routes is therefore of order 1e20-1e23.

Compute what linewidth the coherence claim demands. Coherence length l_c = lambda^2/Delta_lambda. At lambda = 600 nm: Delta_lambda = 400 nm gives l_c = 0.9 um and tau_c = 3 fs; Delta_lambda = 1 nm gives l_c = 0.36 mm and tau_c = 1.2 ps. Coherence across a single cell (10 um) already requires Delta_lambda <= 36 nm; coherence across an organism (10 cm) requires Delta_lambda <= 3.6e-6 nm. The claim is therefore a spectroscopic linewidth claim with a concrete resolution target.

No work in the corpus has resolved a UPE spectrum better than about 10 nm: plant chemiluminescence is characterised by bandpass or cut-off filters (450-850 nm in vitro, red/far-red > 640 nm peaking 700-750 nm in planta; 50 nm bandpass increments in Arabidopsis; 550 nm and 495 nm cut-off ratios in human fingertips; > 650 nm in wounded Spathiphyllum). The narrow-line hypothesis has therefore never been given a chance to fail.

Instrument-side confounds that would fake a narrow feature are documented and controllable: photomultiplier dynode and support-structure light emission with a characterisable spectrum, and the general artifact risk from lacking or improper reference signals in UPE statistics work. The positive/negative control arms are designed against exactly these.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Build a photon-counting Fourier-transform interferometer: light-tight chamber, sample on one port, Michelson with piezo-scanned OPD 0-10 mm, field stop set to the Jacquinot limit for R = 6000, output on a cooled multialkali PMT or an SNSPD. Record the interferogram in photon-arrival-tagged mode over 1e5-1e6 s with interleaved dark, flat-continuum and laser-spiked calibration runs at 0.3%, 1% and 3% injected line fraction to establish the empirical visibility floor. Fourier-transform to a 0.1 nm-resolution spectrum and report the maximum line-to-continuum contrast and its uncertainty. Run the scanning Fabry-Perot variant on the same preparation as an independent instrument check. Pre-register C = 1.2 and OPD = 0.5 mm as the decision thresholds.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Photon-counting Michelson Fourier-transform interferometer (piezo OPD scan 0-10 mm, field stop at Jacquinot limit) with cooled multialkali PMT or SNSPD, 400-900 nm; alternative arm: scanning Fabry-Perot etalon (finesse >= 30, FSR ~2 nm) plus EMCCD photon counter; tunable narrowband diode laser for injected-line positive controls.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: The register carries only second-order intensity claims (H2.g2, H2.sq) and a spectral-shape claim (H11). Nobody has proposed the first-order test, which is the one the coherence claim actually implies and the only one whose sensitivity scales as sqrt(N) rather than as the degeneracy delta - a 1e20 advantage. It restates 'is UPE coherent' as a linewidth measurement with a stated resolution target and an injected-line positive control.

members.statement: The super-Poissonian excess in UPE photocount distributions is generated by radical-chain photon clusters describable as a Neyman type-A cluster point process with cluster rate lambda_c and mean mu photons per initiation event, and mu - not any squeezed-state parameter - is the quantity that responds monotonically to antioxidant dose and to oxygen tension.

hypothesis.statement: The super-Poissonian excess in UPE photocount distributions is generated by radical-chain photon clusters describable as a Neyman type-A cluster point process with cluster rate lambda_c and mean mu photons per initiation event, and mu - not any squeezed-state parameter - is the quantity that responds monotonically to antioxidant dose and to oxygen tension.

scope.population: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii suspensions and aerobic Saccharomyces cerevisiae cultures, with lipid peroxidation initiated by exogenous linoleic acid or by Fenton reagent.
scope.condition: Graded antioxidant series (ascorbate or Trolox at 0, 0.1, 1, 10 mM) crossed with an oxygen-tension series (21% O2, 5% O2, <0.1% O2 by N2 purge); photon arrivals time-tagged at 1 us, three bandpass channels (400-450, 550-600, 700-750 nm).
scope.comparator: Within-run matched dark reference and heat-killed cells driven to the same mean count rate; and, on the identical data, the three-parameter squeezed-state model (r, theta, phi) fitted as in the published human and lichen analyses.
scope.outcome: Fitted (lambda_c, mu) from a joint Neyman type-A fit across bin sizes 1 ms to 10 s, versus fitted (r, theta, phi); dose-response of each parameter set.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: mu shows no monotone dose-response to antioxidant concentration or to pO2 (|Spearman rho| < 0.5 or CI spanning 0), and/or the squeezed-state model beats the cluster model on held-out bin sizes by delta-BIC > 10. Either outcome kills the mechanism claim.
hypothesis.estimand: Spearman rho of mu with antioxidant dose and with pO2 (with 95% CI), and the held-out delta-BIC between the two-parameter Neyman type-A model and the three-parameter squeezed-state model fitted jointly across bin sizes.

rationale.step: Superposition of nonstationary emissions occurring at Poisson-random times produces exactly Neyman type-A photocount distributions (coherent sub-emissions) or generalised Polya-Aeppli distributions (chaotic sub-emissions), with enhanced particle-like noise and increased photon-counting variance. This is a purely classical mechanism that manufactures the 'quantum-looking' excess.

Clustering is directly observed in an ultraweak biological emission: photomultiplier pulses from human breath chemiluminescence arrive in bursts, which the authors attribute to chain reactions, long-lived emitters, or both.

In PMA-stimulated neutrophils the Fano factor of the true UPE signal rises with counting-window size while randomly shuffled surrogates of the same signal do not - the defining signature of a clustered point process rather than of a state of the field.

The chain chemistry is manipulable in exactly these preparations: UPE arises from ROS-driven lipid and protein oxidation via triplet excited carbonyls and singlet oxygen; it falls under anoxia and under topical antioxidants (glutathione, tocopherol, ascorbate, CoQ10), and linoleic-acid-induced emission in Chlamydomonas is suppressed by hydroxyl-radical scavenging (mannitol), by lipoxygenase inhibition (catechol) and by removal of molecular oxygen; wound-induced leaf emission is suppressed under anoxia. Yeast BAL is likewise driven by Fenton-generated ROS and tracks oxygen partial pressure.

The squeezed-state reading rests on a three-parameter fit (signal strength plus r = 0.06, theta = 2.76, phi = 0.64) claimed to reproduce photocount distributions across 50 ms to 6 s bins from 20000 measurements. The cluster model makes the same multi-bin prediction with two parameters and, unlike r/theta/phi, its parameters carry a chemical interpretation that can be perturbed - which is what makes the comparison decisive rather than aesthetic.

Derive the discriminating signature. For a Neyman type-A process the Fano factor at bin T much longer than the cluster duration is F = 1 + mu, independent of lambda_c, while for T much shorter than the cluster duration F tends to 1. The prediction is a sigmoidal F(T) whose plateau height equals mu and whose knee locates the chain duration - a shape no squeezed-state parameterisation predicts. A published seed measurement gives <n> = 27.25 with variance 34.01, i.e. F = 1.25, corresponding to mu = 0.25 detected photons per cluster, i.e. mu/eta = 2.5 emitted photons per initiation at eta = 0.1: a chemically plausible chain yield and a directly falsifiable number.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Time-tag every photon arrival at 1 us from each preparation across the full 4x3 antioxidant-by-oxygen design, three spectral channels, with interleaved dark and heat-killed arms rate-matched by neutral-density attenuation. Build F(T) curves from 1 ms to 10 s and fit, jointly across all bin sizes, (a) a two-parameter Neyman type-A cluster model and (b) the three-parameter squeezed-state model, holding out two bin sizes for model comparison. Report delta-BIC on held-out bins and the dose-response of every fitted parameter. The decisive contrast is that mu must fall with antioxidant dose and with declining pO2 in step with the known suppression of the chain, while r/theta/phi should either move incoherently or track mean rate alone.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Cooled low-dark PMT or SPAD single-photon module with hardware time-tagging at <=1 us (the dual-channel SPAD architecture already demonstrated for human delayed luminescence is sufficient), 350-850 nm, with three bandpass filter channels; gas-tight cuvette with pO2 control and inline oxygen sensor.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: H2.sq is a model-comparison claim with no named physical rival - 'classical mixtures' is not a mechanism. This names the rival (a two-parameter clustered point process derived from radical-chain chemistry), derives its distinctive F(T) sigmoid, converts an existing published Fano factor into a falsifiable chain-yield number, and makes the decisive move the register lacks: requiring the winning model's parameter to move under antioxidant and oxygen titration. It turns a statistics contest into a chemistry experiment.

members.statement: For every standard UPE preparation, the excess Fano factor and Mandel Q measured at bin sizes 1 ms to 10 s are statistically equivalent to those of a spectrally and rate-matched artificial source whose slow-intensity envelope is programmed to reproduce the biological sample's own drift and which is measured in the same chamber at the same temperature.

For day-3 germinating Vigna radiata, broadband UPE arrivals are conditionally Poisson from 1 µs to 1 s once intensity variation slower than 10 s is estimated out-of-sample, so the residual cross-detector g2(τ) remains within 0.05 of unity throughout that lag range.

hypothesis.statement: For every standard UPE preparation, the excess Fano factor and Mandel Q measured at bin sizes 1 ms to 10 s are statistically equivalent to those of a spectrally and rate-matched artificial source whose slow-intensity envelope is programmed to reproduce the biological sample's own drift and which is measured in the same chamber at the same temperature.

scope.population: Germinating Vigna radiata beds, wounded Spathiphyllum or Arabidopsis leaves, and dark-adapted human dorsal hand skin.
scope.condition: Interleaved ABAB runs of the biological sample and a 'sham-luminous' reference: a calibrated LED attenuated ~1e-12 by a traceable neutral-density stack, spectrally shaped to the sample's measured three-band ratios, and driven by an arbitrary waveform that replays the sample's own measured 0.01-1 Hz intensity envelope; chamber temperature clamped to +/-0.05 C.
scope.comparator: The biological arm versus the sham-luminous arm; plus a matched dark arm and a constant-rate (undrifted) artificial arm to separate drift from detector effects.
scope.outcome: F(T)-1 and Mandel Q(T) curves for each arm across 1 ms to 10 s, and their arm-to-arm difference.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The biological arm's excess exceeds the sham-luminous arm's by more than the pre-registered equivalence margin (delta-Q > 0.02 at any bin size, lower 90% bound above the margin). That would establish a biology-specific statistical signature and falsify the claim.
hypothesis.estimand: delta-Q(T) = Q_bio(T) - Q_sham(T) with 90% CI, evaluated jointly across bin sizes 1 ms to 10 s and tested by two-one-sided-tests against the pre-registered equivalence margin.

rationale.step: The shape of a measured UPE photocount distribution is a convolution of the background distribution with the sample's distribution, so no excess is attributable to the sample unless a reference arm reproduces the background's own fluctuation structure - which a dark run, being non-luminous, cannot do.

The failure mode is not hypothetical: in 2026 the large reported extracranial 'brain UPE' signals were shown to be explicable by background light contamination once properly dark conditions were imposed, with the additional point that sub-600 nm photons are strongly attenuated by scalp and skull while longer wavelengths fall outside the PMT's effective response.

The methodological review of biological autoluminescence statistics states directly that there is little experimental work showing any difference of the signal from random Poisson noise and that several prior works were prone to artifacts due to lacking or improper reference signals.

Detector-side generators of correlated counts are documented in the corpus: photomultiplier dynode and support-structure light emission producing afterpulses, afterpulse spectra that degrade photon-correlation spectroscopy, and EM-CCD sensitivity to blackbody radiation above 50 C in a regime where detector noise already dominates source photon noise.

The observables at stake are exactly the published ones: Fano factor and g2(0) computed at 50 ms bins from a human hand, non-zero kurtosis distinguishing diabetic from healthy subjects, and F = 1.25 from germinating seeds. All were reported without a luminous, drift-matched reference arm.

Compute how little drift is needed to fake the whole literature. For a doubly stochastic (Cox) process whose rate fluctuates with relative variance sigma_I^2 over the bin, the Mandel parameter is Q = <n>*sigma_I^2. At <n> = 5 counts per bin, an intensity drift of only 6% RMS reproduces Q = 0.02, i.e. F = 1.004; at <n> = 27 (the published seed case) a 10% RMS drift reproduces F = 1.27. Percent-level drift is unremarkable in a live sample, a warming chamber or a settling PMT, so the entire published excess is accounted for without any assumption about the state of the field. The sham-luminous arm makes that drift an experimental variable instead of an interpretation.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: For each preparation, first record the biological arm with photon time-tagging and extract its 0.01-1 Hz intensity envelope and its three-band spectral ratios. Then synthesise the sham-luminous arm: an LED attenuated through a traceable neutral-density stack to the same mean count rate, spectrally shaped to the same band ratios, and amplitude-modulated by the recorded envelope. Run ABAB interleaving (biological, sham-luminous, dark, constant-rate artificial) for at least 20 cycles per preparation in a temperature-clamped chamber, with detector afterpulse and dead-time characterisation performed on the same day. Compute F(T) and Q(T) on all arms and test delta-Q(T) by TOST against the pre-registered margin. Report the drift RMS actually required to match, as a check on the Q = <n>*sigma_I^2 arithmetic.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Cooled low-dark PMT (300-850 nm, <10 dark counts/s) with hardware time-tagging; calibrated LED attenuated ~1e-12 through a traceable neutral-density stack with arbitrary-waveform drive and three-channel spectral shaping; temperature-clamped (+/-0.05 C) light-tight chamber; separate afterpulse/dead-time characterisation bench.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: H2 and H2.sq are catalogued 'with explicit nulls', but the null is a statistical model rather than a physical control arm. This names the missing control - an intensity-, spectrum- and drift-matched luminous sham - and supplies the arithmetic (Q = <n>*sigma_I^2) showing that a few percent of intensity drift regenerates the entire published excess. If it holds, H2.sq is decided negatively without ever fitting a squeezed state; if it fails, the field finally has a positive result that survives its own instrument.

members.statement: No photocount or temporal-complexity feature of UPE - Fano factor, Mandel Q, kurtosis, Hurst/fractional-Brownian exponent, diffusion-entropy scaling exponent, or entropy-weighted spectral fractal dimension - adds more than 0.02 AUC out-of-sample to a classifier of biological state that already contains log mean count rate plus chamber temperature and background rate.

hypothesis.statement: No photocount or temporal-complexity feature of UPE - Fano factor, Mandel Q, kurtosis, Hurst/fractional-Brownian exponent, diffusion-entropy scaling exponent, or entropy-weighted spectral fractal dimension - adds more than 0.02 AUC out-of-sample to a classifier of biological state that already contains log mean count rate plus chamber temperature and background rate.

scope.population: Two pre-registered discrimination tasks, each with an independent held-out cohort acquired after the model is frozen: (a) glioblastoma versus astrocyte cell cultures; (b) viable versus degenerated or frozen mouse embryos, and as a second clinical arm healthy versus type-2-diabetic human hand skin.
scope.condition: Blinded analysis of fixed-length photon-count time series (identical acquisition length, bin grid and spectral band across classes), with chamber temperature and interleaved dark-reference rate logged as covariates.
scope.comparator: An intensity-only baseline model containing log mean count rate plus the same covariates, fitted and evaluated on identical folds.
scope.outcome: delta-AUC on the held-out cohort between the full-feature model and the intensity-only baseline.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: delta-AUC > 0.02 with a lower 95% confidence bound above 0 on a genuinely held-out cohort. That would show photocount statistics carry state information beyond intensity and would falsify the claim.
hypothesis.estimand: delta-AUC (held-out) between full-feature and intensity-only models, with 95% CI from nested cross-fitting plus an external cohort; reported per task and pooled.

rationale.step: Multiple groups report that temporal-statistical features separate biological states: diffusion entropy analysis separating astrocyte from glioblastoma cultures; anomalous DEA scaling appearing with germinating seeds present but ordinary scaling in dark counts; a fractional-Brownian negative-memory signature in mung-bean autoluminescence; an entropy-weighted spectral fractal dimension distinguishing living from degenerated and frozen from fresh mouse embryos; non-zero kurtosis in healthy and diabetic photocount distributions; and spectral power density profiles yielding 90% discriminant accuracy for malignancy.

In none of those studies is the comparison made against an intensity-matched baseline, yet mean intensity is itself an established correlate of the same states: tumour cells emit more than non-malignant cells, stressed cells emit more than healthy ones, and UPE intensity tracks ROS production and oxidative status generally.

The one UPE study in the corpus that used surrogate randomisation for a physiological correlation found the correlations to be temporary, drifting in phase and frequency - the behaviour expected of a shared slow covariate rather than of a stable state-specific feature.

Show the confound is structural, not incidental. Every listed feature is a functional of the same intensity time series and is monotonically biased by mean rate. For a Cox process, Q = <n>*sigma_I^2, so any class difference in mean rate propagates directly into Q and F. Likewise, an estimated Hurst or DEA scaling exponent is pulled toward the uncorrelated value 0.5 as the Poisson shot component grows relative to the rate-fluctuation component, i.e. as <n> falls; the dark-count arm returning ordinary scaling while the seed arm returns anomalous scaling is exactly what this bias predicts when the two arms differ in mean rate. Matching or adjusting on log mean rate is therefore the minimal control, and it has been applied in none of the cited works.

The critical review already frames the whole controversy as one about statistical properties rather than intensity and spectrum, on which there is consensus; so the practical question 'can photocount statistics ever decide anything' is precisely whether these features survive an intensity-matched baseline.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Pre-register the feature list, the baseline covariates, the equivalence threshold (delta-AUC = 0.02) and the analysis code before any held-out data are acquired. Acquire matched-length photon-count time series for both classes in each task under identical bin grid, spectral band and acquisition length, with in-chamber temperature and an interleaved dark-reference channel recorded continuously. Fit the intensity-only baseline and the full-feature model on the development cohort with nested cross-fitting, freeze both, then evaluate once on the externally acquired held-out cohort. Report delta-AUC with CI, plus a rate-matched subsample analysis in which classes are trimmed to overlapping log-mean-rate distributions. No new detector is needed; the claim is a design-and-analysis claim and is testable on re-analysis of any existing dataset that retained raw time series and rate logs.
