hypothesis.required_instrument: Cooled PMT photon counter with time tagging or >=1 kHz binned readout, 350-850 nm, plus in-chamber thermistor and an interleaved dark-reference channel; no new detector class required.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: The register's out-of-sample claims (H3, H8, H9) concern delayed-luminescence decay parameters, surface intensity and crop vigour, and H11 concerns spectral distribution. None asks whether photocount and temporal-complexity features - the exact observables the coherence debate is conducted in - survive an intensity-matched baseline. This converts 'can photocount statistics ever decide?' into a pre-registerable prediction with a numeric threshold, and identifies the specific estimator bias (rate-dependent pull of Hurst/DEA exponents toward 0.5) that would produce the published pattern with no biology in it.

members.statement: The photocount 'squeezed-state' parameters reported for human surface UPE can be reproduced, within the range published across anatomical sites, from a spectrally matched incoherent artificial source viewed through a tissue-mimicking scattering phantom of matched reduced-scattering and absorption coefficients, so those parameters are set by propagation and detection geometry rather than by the emitting state.

hypothesis.statement: The photocount 'squeezed-state' parameters reported for human surface UPE can be reproduced, within the range published across anatomical sites, from a spectrally matched incoherent artificial source viewed through a tissue-mimicking scattering phantom of matched reduced-scattering and absorption coefficients, so those parameters are set by propagation and detection geometry rather than by the emitting state.

scope.population: An artificial incoherent source (attenuated LED, three-channel spectrally shaped to the reported human skin UPE band ratios) placed behind Intralipid or TiO2-silicone phantoms with reduced scattering coefficient 1-3 mm-1 and absorption 0.01-0.1 mm-1 at 600-750 nm and thicknesses 0.5-3 mm; contrasted with dark-adapted human dorsal hand and palm.
scope.condition: Identical detector, chamber, spectral window and acquisition protocol as the published human analyses: 300-800 nm broadband detection, contiguous bins of 50, 100, 200, 300 and 500 ms, 20000 measurements per run, background measured and subtracted the same way.
scope.comparator: The published human parameter ranges (signal strength plus r ~ 0.06, theta ~ 2.76, phi ~ 0.64, and the site-wise profiles reported across 12 anatomical sites), and an unfiltered artificial source with no phantom.
scope.outcome: Fitted squeezed parameters (r, theta, phi) and Fano factor / g2(0) for the phantom-filtered artificial light, as a function of phantom optical properties and thickness.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The phantom-filtered artificial source yields parameters outside the published human range at every phantom setting - for instance r below one third or above three times the reported 0.06, with the human range excluded at 95% - which would show that the human parameters carry source-specific information that propagation cannot manufacture.
hypothesis.estimand: The fraction of phantom configurations whose fitted (r, theta, phi) fall inside the convex hull of the published human site-wise parameter set, and the minimum |delta-r| between any phantom configuration and the reported human value.

rationale.step: Human surface photocount analyses report squeezed-state parameters recovered from broadband, large-area, long-duration acquisitions - r = 0.06, theta = 2.76, phi = 0.64 from 20000 bins over 50-500 ms in a lichen, and site-wise 'profiles' of nine such properties across 12 anatomical sites in humans, with Fano factor and g2(0) readouts from the hand at 50 ms bins and squeezed-state descriptions of the H2O2-stimulated skin response.

The same preparation has yielded the opposite conclusion from the same class of measurement: hand UPE was reported to lack the usual coherence because of the large area and the long measurement time. A parameter that flips sign with acquisition geometry is a geometry parameter until proven otherwise.

Surface UPE in humans is a diffusely propagated signal, not a direct view of an emitter: relating an internal photogenic source to surface fluence requires a photon-diffusion model with an extrapolated zero-boundary condition, and sub-600 nm photons are strongly attenuated by overlying tissue while longer wavelengths sit at the edge of PMT sensitivity.

Derive why the phantom must reproduce the fit. Multiple scattering through a slab with reduced scattering coefficient 2 mm-1 randomises transverse phase at the exit face and fixes the collected spatial mode count M through the speckle size and the collection etendue. Since for any chaotic field g2(0)-1 = 1/M, and the fitted squeezed parameter r enters the photocount distribution only through the same second-moment excess, r is a monotone reparameterisation of a quantity determined by M together with the slow-drift envelope. The phantom arm reproduces both by construction - M by matched optical properties and geometry, the drift envelope by programmed modulation - so if the human r is a transport quantity the phantom must land inside the human range.

The measured photocount shape is in any case a convolution of the background distribution with the sample distribution, so an arm matched in rate, drift and mode count is the correct negative control for any fitted state parameter; this control has never been run.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Fabricate a phantom series (Intralipid suspensions and TiO2-silicone slabs) characterised independently by spatially resolved or time-resolved diffuse reflectance to fix reduced scattering 1-3 mm-1 and absorption 0.01-0.1 mm-1 at 600-750 nm, thicknesses 0.5-3 mm. Behind each, place a three-channel LED attenuated to the count rate measured from dorsal hand skin and amplitude-modulated with a drift envelope recorded from a real human run. Acquire with the identical detector, spectral window, bin ladder (50-500 ms) and 20000-bin protocol as the published human analyses, including the same background measurement and subtraction. Fit the published squeezed-state model to each phantom run, and to fresh human dorsal-hand and palm runs recorded the same week. Report where the phantom parameters fall relative to the human convex hull, and the dependence of r on phantom thickness and scattering coefficient. Pre-register the exclusion criterion.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Cooled PMT photon counter (300-850 nm) with time tagging; Intralipid and TiO2-silicone tissue phantoms characterised by time-resolved or spatially resolved diffuse reflectance; attenuated three-channel LED with programmable drift; the same light-tight chamber and acquisition software used for the human arm.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: H2.sq is stated as a model-fit comparison against classical mixtures, and H2/H6/H8 all rest silently on human surface measurements. This exposes the propagation assumption underneath them: the human-surface squeezed-state literature never established that its fitted parameters are properties of the source rather than of transport through several millimetres of scattering tissue. The tissue phantom is the missing negative control, it is buildable with off-the-shelf materials, and it converts a state claim into a measurable transport claim by predicting that r should vary with phantom thickness and scattering coefficient alone.

members.statement: For day-3 germinating Vigna radiata, source-intrinsic second- and third-order factorial cumulants of 400–750 nm UPE obey the calibrated Bernoulli-thinning laws κ2(η)=η²κ2(1) and κ3(η)=η³κ3(1) across optical transmissions η=0.10, 0.25, 0.50 and 1.00.

hypothesis.statement: For day-3 germinating Vigna radiata, source-intrinsic second- and third-order factorial cumulants of 400–750 nm UPE obey the calibrated Bernoulli-thinning laws κ2(η)=η²κ2(1) and κ3(η)=η³κ3(1) across optical transmissions η=0.10, 0.25, 0.50 and 1.00.

scope.population: Independent batches of day-3 germinating Vigna radiata seeds
scope.condition: Dark-adapted spontaneous emission recorded in stationary 30-minute blocks
scope.comparator: Empty chamber and intensity-matched Poisson LED measured through the same four transmissions
scope.outcome: Detector-corrected second- and third-order factorial cumulants of counts in preregistered 50 ms, 200 ms and 1 s bins

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The biological-sample cumulants reject the thinning laws at the preregistered 0.01 level or show the same transmission-dependent residuals as detector controls, indicating that the apparent statistics cannot be assigned to the emitted field.
hypothesis.estimand: The joint chi-square lack-of-fit statistic for κr(η)=η^rκr(1), r=2,3, after propagation of quantum-efficiency, dark-count, crosstalk and dead-time uncertainties

rationale.step: Photocount distributions have been measured in germinating mung beans, and their form changes with bin size.
The critical review identifies detector nonideality as a central obstacle and argues that detectors closer to ideal may resolve UPE statistical properties.
Calibrated statistical detector models have already enabled visible-light detection below 30 photons s−1 cm−2 while explicitly treating quantum efficiency and detector noise.

Independent detection with probability η binomially thins photon number, so the r-th factorial cumulant scales as η^r; failure of this scaling localizes the anomaly to the detector or an unmodelled transmission-dependent background.
The seed brief makes characterized quantum efficiency and dead-time prerequisites for interpreting photocount statistics.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Place calibrated neutral-density filters before all detection optics, randomize filter order within each stationary recording block, and acquire photon-number histograms simultaneously with environmental and empty-chamber controls. Estimate factorial cumulants with a preregistered detector-response matrix calibrated using a pulsed Poisson source; test the two thinning equations jointly at every bin width and in held-out seed batches.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Calibrated visible-sensitive multi-pixel SNSPD or other photon-number-resolving array covering 400–750 nm, with independently measured wavelength-dependent efficiency, pixel crosstalk, timing jitter and dead-time
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This adds an intervention-based detector-validity test: unlike H2.g2 or H2.sq, it requires a purported optical-state signature to transform correctly under known loss before any biological interpretation is allowed.

members.statement: Aerobic wound-induced Spathiphyllum UPE is multimode thermal in the chlorophyll band: narrowing detection from 650–720 nm to 669.95–670.05 nm will increase g2(0) by at least 0.10 and reveal a picosecond bunching envelope absent under anoxia.

hypothesis.statement: Aerobic wound-induced Spathiphyllum UPE is multimode thermal in the chlorophyll band: narrowing detection from 650–720 nm to 669.95–670.05 nm will increase g2(0) by at least 0.10 and reveal a picosecond bunching envelope absent under anoxia.

scope.population: Mature Spathiphyllum leaves from independently grown plants
scope.condition: Mechanical wounding after two hours of dark adaptation, measured separately under air and nitrogen
scope.comparator: The same leaves before wounding, wounded leaves under anoxia, broadband 650–720 nm detection, and an attenuated coherent laser calibration
scope.outcome: Cross-detector g2(τ) near zero delay and its dependence on optical bandwidth

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: Narrowing the band produces less than a 0.10 increase in g2(0), no reproducible bunching envelope, or an identical feature in anoxic and detector-only controls.
hypothesis.estimand: Δg2=g2,narrow(0)−g2,broad(0), together with the fitted bunching-envelope half-width after deconvolution of detector jitter

rationale.step: Aerobic wounded Spathiphyllum leaves emit predominantly above 650 nm, whereas anoxia suppresses wound-induced emission; broadband count distributions in several states approximately followed Poisson laws.

The UPE literature notes that a many-mode thermal photocount distribution approaches a Poisson distribution, making coherent and thermal emissions difficult to distinguish under broad mode collection.
At λ=670 nm and Δλ=0.10 nm, λ²/(cΔλ) is approximately 15 ps, setting the order of the expected first-order coherence time and thermal g2 bunching width.

For M independent equally populated thermal modes, g2(0)=1+1/M; spectral and spatial mode restriction should therefore increase bunching, whereas a coherent state retains g2(0)=1 under passive filtering.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Collect emission from a standardized array of wounded leaves into a stabilized Hanbury Brown–Twiss system. Alternate a 650–720 nm filter with a 0.10 nm tunable etalon centered at 670 nm, hold collection étendue fixed, and integrate coincidences over repeated leaves. Pre-register a jitter-convolved thermal bunching model and coherent g2=1 model, with filter order randomized and anoxic leaves processed identically.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Two high-efficiency red-sensitive SNSPDs with approximately 10–20 ps timing jitter, a time-correlated single-photon counter, and switchable 650–720 nm and 0.10 nm filters centered near 670 nm
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: Instead of merely asking whether g2(0) differs from one, this tests the specific multimode-averaging explanation for Poisson-like UPE through a predicted bandwidth-dependent bunching law.

members.statement: The squeezed-state claim for Xanthoria parietina implies a phase-sensitive minimum quadrature variance no greater than 0.92 of shot noise in a mode-matched 300–800 nm optical mode.

hypothesis.statement: The squeezed-state claim for Xanthoria parietina implies a phase-sensitive minimum quadrature variance no greater than 0.92 of shot noise in a mode-matched 300–800 nm optical mode.

scope.population: Viable, dark-adapted Xanthoria parietina thalli prepared as in the published photocount study
scope.condition: Spontaneous emission measured in repeated stationary intervals, with the local-oscillator spectrum and spatial mode matched to the measured UPE
scope.comparator: Killed lichen, empty chamber, blocked signal port, and an attenuation-matched coherent calibration source
scope.outcome: Minimum balanced-homodyne quadrature variance normalized to contemporaneous shot noise

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: All preregistered quadrature phases have variance at or above 0.98 of shot noise after correcting electronic noise, loss and mode mismatch, or any apparent reduction also occurs in blocked-port controls.
hypothesis.estimand: The minimum loss-corrected quadrature variance Vmin/Vshot and its one-sided 95% confidence bound

rationale.step: Photocount distributions from Xanthoria parietina were reported to be reproduced over 50 ms–6 s by a squeezed-state model with squeezing parameter r=0.06.
Interpretations of UPE photocount statistics as coherent or squeezed states remain controversial and are not generally accepted.

For an ideal squeezed quadrature, Vmin/Vshot=e^(−2r); substituting r=0.06 gives e^(−0.12)=0.887, so a 0.92 threshold allows limited calibrated loss while remaining a direct prediction of the reported parameter.

A classical mixture can imitate some photon-number distributions, but a reproducible quadrature variance below shot noise is a phase-sensitive nonclassical signature independent of fitting the same count histogram.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: First measure the lichen's spectral and spatial emission profile, then shape a weak local oscillator to that mode and scan quadrature phase in randomized blocks. Calibrate shot noise before and after every biological block, quantify total optical loss and mode overlap, and perform the preregistered one-sided variance test on held-out thalli.
hypothesis.required_instrument: High-quantum-efficiency balanced homodyne receiver with a spectrally shaped local oscillator covering the detected 300–800 nm UPE mode, shot-noise clearance monitoring and low-noise visible photodiodes
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This advances beyond H2.sq by demanding the independent phase-sensitive consequence of the published squeezing parameter rather than another comparison of photon-count models.

members.statement: Aerobic wound-induced Spathiphyllum emission at 660–680 nm has intrinsic spatial first-order coherence exceeding that produced by passive filtering of an equally extended incoherent source, with excess |g1| of at least 0.10 at a 100 µm source-plane shear.

hypothesis.statement: Aerobic wound-induced Spathiphyllum emission at 660–680 nm has intrinsic spatial first-order coherence exceeding that produced by passive filtering of an equally extended incoherent source, with excess |g1| of at least 0.10 at a 100 µm source-plane shear.

scope.population: Mature Spathiphyllum leaves from independently grown plants
scope.condition: Mechanical wounding after two hours of dark adaptation in air, analyzed in preregistered quasi-stationary decay windows
scope.comparator: Pre-wound leaves, wounded leaves under anoxia, and an intensity- and geometry-matched incoherent calibration source passed through identical optics
scope.outcome: Interferometric fringe visibility converted to |g1| after correcting arm imbalance and subtracting the incoherent-source prediction

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: At 100 µm shear, the upper 95% confidence bound for excess |g1| is below 0.10 or the observed visibility is fully reproduced by the filtered incoherent calibration source.
hypothesis.estimand: Excess spatial coherence Δ|g1|=|g1|leaf−|g1|matched-incoherent at 100 µm shear

rationale.step: Wound-induced Spathiphyllum emission is oxygen-dependent and concentrated above 650 nm, providing a defined high-signal biological and spectral reference.
The UPE literature's claims about coherence and the interpretation of photocount statistics are explicitly controversial.
Photon-counting EMCCD systems with calibrated detector-noise models can detect visible fluxes below 30 photons s−1 cm−2, supporting long-exposure interferometric imaging at UPE levels.
For two interferometer arms with intensities I1 and I2, visibility V=[2√(I1I2)/(I1+I2)]|g1|; measuring both arm intensities therefore permits a checkable estimate of first-order coherence.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Image a fixed leaf region through a stabilized lateral-shearing interferometer at several source-plane separations, with 100 µm designated as primary. Measure each arm separately, phase-step the interferometer, and estimate visibility from repeated wound-decay windows. Run an extended incoherent source matched to the leaf's measured intensity map and spectrum through the identical aperture and filter to quantify coherence introduced by the optics alone.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Back-illuminated photon-counting EMCCD or qCMOS camera with a phase-stepped lateral-shearing interferometer and a 660–680 nm bandpass filter
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This operationalizes coherence as first-order spatial coherence, which neither H2.g2 nor H2.sq measures, and explicitly subtracts coherence created by spectral and spatial filtering.

members.statement: In every preparation with a published optical-only donor-to-receiver effect, an artificial source calibrated to reproduce the donor's absolute spectral photon fluence rate at the receiver plane fails to reproduce the effect, and the artificial fluence rate needed to reproduce half the reported effect exceeds the donor's own fluence rate by at least a factor of 1000.

hypothesis.statement: In every preparation with a published optical-only donor-to-receiver effect, an artificial source calibrated to reproduce the donor's absolute spectral photon fluence rate at the receiver plane fails to reproduce the effect, and the artificial fluence rate needed to reproduce half the reported effect exceeds the donor's own fluence rate by at least a factor of 1000.

scope.population: Paramecium caudatum population pairs separated by glass or quartz cuvette walls (Fels preparation), and isolated MCF7 / MCF10A mitochondria in adjacent optically coupled cuvettes (Frontiers 2023 preparation)
scope.condition: receiver exposed to a spectrally and absolutely dose-matched artificial source (programmable LED array / monochromator, 300-800 nm, matched to within +/-30 percent in every 50 nm band and matched in temporal profile) in place of the live donor, plus an ND-attenuation ladder spanning 10^0 to 10^6 times the donor fluence
scope.comparator: live donor across the identical optical window; opaque-shutter sham with identical thermal and gas conditions; medium-only chamber
scope.outcome: the original published endpoint - cell division rate and vacuole/energy uptake for Paramecium; oxygen consumption rate for the mitochondrial preparation

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: R <= 1: artificial illumination dose-matched to the donor reproduces at least half the published donor effect size, establishing photon sufficiency and killing this hypothesis.
hypothesis.estimand: R = F_half / F_donor, where F_half is the artificial-source photon fluence rate (photons cm^-2 s^-1 integrated 300-800 nm) that produces 50 percent of the published donor effect size, and F_donor is the absolutely calibrated donor fluence rate at the receiver plane. Claim: R >= 10^3.

rationale.step: Positive optical-only donor-to-receiver effects are on record in exactly these two preparations, with glass-versus-quartz window contrasts and physically separated cuvettes; the mitochondrial study explicitly leaves the carrier unidentified and calls for UPE characterisation.

The field's own signal-to-noise analysis argues that emitted intensity plus ambient noise makes receiver-side detection implausible, but it is a calculation over literature values and never substitutes a calibrated source for the donor inside the same preparation.
Reported spontaneous UPE intensities span a few to about 10^4 photons cm^-2 s^-1 over roughly 260-800 nm, with 10 to 10^4 photons s^-1 cm^-2 quoted specifically for the UV from active cells.

Take the most generous published emission, 10^4 photons cm^-2 s^-1, sustained for 24 h = 8.64e4 s. Accumulated fluence = 8.64e8 photons cm^-2. At 450 nm the photon energy is hc/lambda = (6.626e-34 * 2.998e8) / 450e-9 = 4.41e-19 J, so the 24 h energy fluence is 8.64e8 * 4.41e-19 = 3.81e-10 J cm^-2.

Documented photobiomodulation effects on proliferation in cultured cells require of order 1-10 J cm^-2 at the target, with peak proliferative benefit near 2 J cm^-2 and a characterised blue/green anti-proliferative effect at 3 J cm^-2.

Ratio of the weakest documented photobiological dose to the entire 24 h UPE budget: 1 J cm^-2 / 3.81e-10 J cm^-2 = 2.6e9. The claim R >= 10^3 is therefore conservative by about six orders of magnitude relative to established photobiology dose-response.
The field itself names absolutely calibrated photon budgets, showing the receiver plausibly gets enough photons, as the criterion that would settle the functional-role question.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Rebuild one published DCI preparation with a removable donor chamber. Step 1: map the donor's absolute spectral photon fluence at the exact receiver plane with a traceably calibrated photon-counting PMT plus a cooled qCMOS for spatial uniformity, in 50 nm bands from 300 to 800 nm, over the full exposure window. Step 2: replace the donor with a programmable LED/monochromator source driven to reproduce that map within +/-30 percent per band and matched in temporal envelope, verified in situ at the receiver plane. Step 3: run a blinded, pre-registered ND ladder at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, 10^3, 10^4, 10^5, 10^6 times the donor fluence plus opaque sham, with the receiver endpoint scored by an operator blind to arm. Fit the dose-response and read off F_half. Multi-lab, with the calibration transfer standard physically shipped between labs.
hypothesis.required_instrument: NIST-traceable photon-counting PMT (bialkali, 300-650 nm) with calibrated quartz optics; back-illuminated qCMOS or EMCCD (ORCA-Quest class, as used for mouse-embryo UPE) for receiver-plane fluence mapping; programmable multi-LED / monochromator source with calibrated neutral-density ladder spanning 10^0-10^6, 300-800 nm
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: Register H4b states the receiver-side null bare. This replaces it with one calibrated ratio R that is informative whichever way it falls: a quantitative upper bound on receiver photosensitivity if large, an immediate mechanism if it is at or below 1. No study in the corpus has substituted a dose-matched artificial source for the donor inside a preparation that reported a positive effect.

members.statement: Brightness conservation caps any reflective or focusing geometry at roughly twice the photon fluence a receiver gets facing the bare donor, so the reflector-specific biological effects reported in focused-chamber research cannot be dose-driven optical effects.

hypothesis.statement: Brightness conservation caps any reflective or focusing geometry at roughly twice the photon fluence a receiver gets facing the bare donor, so the reflector-specific biological effects reported in focused-chamber research cannot be dose-driven optical effects.

scope.population: adult murine subventricular-zone neural stem cell / neurosphere cultures, and Caenorhabditis elegans cohorts, in concave or sector reflective chambers of the type reviewed in the focused-reflective-chamber literature
scope.condition: reflective chamber with optical return gain G measured in situ with a traceably calibrated isotropic micro-source, per 50 nm band
scope.comparator: geometrically identical blackened chamber (G approximately 1) matched for wall thermal emissivity, gas volume and evaporation; plus a direct-exposure arm in which donor emission is doubled by doubling donor biomass at fixed distance
scope.outcome: neuronal differentiation fraction by immunocytochemistry, neurosphere count, and median C. elegans lifespan

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: Measured in-situ G exceeds 2, or effect size rises monotonically with log G and vanishes at G approximately 1 - either result falsifies the etendue-bound claim and supports optical mediation.
hypothesis.estimand: G = (photon fluence at the receiver plane with the reflector) / (without it), measured per 50 nm band with a calibrated in-situ source; and beta = the slope of biological effect size on log G. Claim: G <= 2 and beta indistinguishable from 0 at alpha = 0.05 with pre-registered power.

rationale.step: Concave and sector reflective chambers are claimed to focus ultraweak biophoton emission and to alter neural stem cell UPE and differentiation, and to extend C. elegans lifespan by 19-30 percent; the review that collects these reports itself flags absent blinding, small samples, inconsistent methods and no independent replication.

The primary neural stem cell experiment that this literature rests on reports the opposite of the summary: the mirror did not significantly increase UPE either before or after differentiation, and neither mirror nor silver nanoparticles changed neurosphere number, while silver nanoparticles alone raised UPE and increased neuronal differentiation by 44 percent. The reflector arm was the null arm.

Mirror-based self-exposure ('autooptic') geometry has separately been claimed to boost a genoprotective drug effect in HepG2 cells, using the same untested premise that a mirror materially raises the delivered optical dose.

Etendue / brightness conservation: no passive optic can raise the radiance L of a source. The maximum irradiance deliverable to a receiver from a Lambertian source of radiance L is pi*L, attained when the receiver collects a full hemisphere. A receiver already facing the donor across a short gap collects approximately one hemisphere, so a rear mirror of reflectivity R_m can add at most the back hemisphere: G <= 1 + R_m <= 1.9 for R_m = 0.9. Curvature redistributes but cannot exceed this bound.

Combining with the fluence arithmetic of Q3-1: the baseline optical dose in these chambers is about 10^9 below the weakest documented photobiological threshold, so a factor <= 2 change could only produce a 19-30 percent lifespan shift if the receiver dose-response were a step function sited at 10^-9 of every measured photobiological threshold.
Measured photobiological dose-response is biphasic and shallow near threshold rather than step-like, over exactly the fluence range where thresholds have been characterised.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Take one reflective chamber with a published positive result. First, with no biology present, place a traceably calibrated fibre-coupled isotropic micro-source at the donor position and a calibrated PMT/qCMOS at the receiver position, and measure G per 50 nm band from 300 to 800 nm - this number has never been reported. Second, fabricate a matched blackened chamber with identical geometry, wall thermal emissivity, gas volume and evaporation rate, and instrument both with thermocouples and an IR camera to bound the radiative-thermal confound. Third, run the biological endpoint blinded and randomised across a graded gain series (blackened, half-silvered, fully silvered, silvered plus focusing) whose G values were measured in step one, and regress effect size on log G. A photon-mediated effect must show beta > 0 and must vanish at G approximately 1.
hypothesis.required_instrument: traceably calibrated fibre-coupled isotropic micro-source (300-800 nm) for in-situ gain mapping; photon-counting PMT plus cooled qCMOS for UPE and receiver-plane fluence; thermocouples and IR camera for the thermal-confound bound
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: Introduces a hard physical bound - conservation of radiance - that the entire focused-reflector and autooptic literature assumes away and has never measured, converts 'the mirror concentrates biophotons' into a measurable gain G with a predicted ceiling, and surfaces a concrete contradiction between the review's summary of the reflective-chamber evidence and its own most rigorous primary source, which found the mirror inert.

members.statement: The UPE photon yield per oxidation event is fixed by chemistry and not by physiological state: within a defined preparation, at matched independently measured oxidative flux, no physiological state changes photons emitted per oxidation event by more than twofold in any spectral band.

hypothesis.statement: The UPE photon yield per oxidation event is fixed by chemistry and not by physiological state: within a defined preparation, at matched independently measured oxidative flux, no physiological state changes photons emitted per oxidation event by more than twofold in any spectral band.

scope.population: one mammalian cell line (MCF10A) plus mitochondria isolated from the same line, and Arabidopsis thaliana rosette leaves
scope.condition: physiological state pairs contrasted at deliberately matched oxidative flux - proliferating versus contact-inhibited; pre- versus post-mechanical-wounding titrated to equal H2O2 efflux; antimycin-inhibited versus uninhibited; normoxic versus mildly hypoxic at equal peroxidation rate
scope.comparator: a cell-free chemical reference emitter (thermolysis of 3,3,4,4-tetramethyl-1,2-dioxetane) run through the identical optical chain, fixing the instrument's absolute photons-per-event calibration
scope.outcome: Phi = band-resolved photon emission rate (photons s^-1 per 50 nm bin, 350-850 nm) divided by simultaneously measured oxidative flux (H2O2 efflux by Amplex Red, oxygen consumption rate, malondialdehyde / TBARS)

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: Some state pair changes Phi by more than twofold at matched oxidative flux, in a blinded pre-registered comparison - showing the radiative step itself is under biological control and falsifying the pure-byproduct reading of the emitter.
hypothesis.estimand: max over state pairs and bands of |log2(Phi_state1 / Phi_state2)| at matched oxidative flux. Claim: < 1.

rationale.step: The field currently reads UPE as a monotone proxy for ROS and oxidative flux, and proposes it as a perturbance-free oxidation monitor and a non-invasive mitochondrial-dysfunction assay - a reading that presupposes a fixed conversion efficiency without ever measuring one.

The emitting chemistry is identified: lipid hydroperoxide decomposition through dioxetane intermediates to excited triplet carbonyls, with triplet-triplet energy transfer to ground-state O2 producing singlet oxygen; wound-induced emission is abolished under anoxia; in Acanthamoeba, mitochondrial and peroxisomal substrates gave no increase in emission while superoxide-generating conditions did.

Phi is a product of three separable branch ratios: the fraction of peroxidation events routed through dioxetane, the triplet yield of the carbonyl, and the radiative branching against non-radiative quenching. All three depend on local solvent polarity, oxygen tension and quencher concentration - variables that cells actively regulate - so invariance of Phi is a substantive empirical claim rather than a definitional one.

The radiative branch is demonstrably manipulable independently of the oxidative flux: dietary alpha-tocopherol and in-vitro radical scavengers quench tissue ultraweak chemiluminescence, and the emission spectrum shows discrete singlet-oxygen-like peaks that a change in quencher environment would reweight.

The seed question is precisely whether UPE is a metabolic byproduct or carries a functional role; a regulated emission efficiency at the emitter is what a signal looks like before any receiver is invoked, and it is testable without solving the receiver problem at all.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Build a thermostatted light-tight chamber with a photon-counting PMT behind a motorised 50 nm bandpass wheel (350-850 nm), co-registered with an optical oxygen sensor and an in-chamber Amplex Red readout, plus destructive TBARS sampling at fixed times. Calibrate absolute photons per event by running tetramethyl-1,2-dioxetane thermolysis at known concentration through the identical chain. For each state pair, titrate the treatment so that the two states have statistically indistinguishable H2O2 efflux and oxygen consumption, then compare Phi band by band. Pre-register the matching tolerance and the twofold decision boundary; blind the analyst to state labels.
hypothesis.required_instrument: photon-counting PMT (bialkali/multialkali, 350-850 nm) with motorised 50 nm bandpass filter wheel in a thermostatted dark chamber; optical O2 sensor and Amplex Red plate readout in-chamber; chemical reference emitter for absolute photons-per-event calibration
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: Register H4a asks what fraction of UPE intensity known oxidative chemistry accounts for. This asks the different and decisive question - whether the conversion efficiency from oxidation event to emitted photon is itself under biological control. Invariance settles the emitter side for byproduct; modulation is emitter-side evidence for function that does not depend on any receiver claim surviving.

members.statement: Donor UPE per unit metabolic rate is not modulated by the presence, viability, or optical accessibility of a receiver population - emitters do not regulate emission in a receiver-contingent way.

hypothesis.statement: Donor UPE per unit metabolic rate is not modulated by the presence, viability, or optical accessibility of a receiver population - emitters do not regulate emission in a receiver-contingent way.

scope.population: Paramecium caudatum donor populations, and isolated MCF7 / MCF10A mitochondria in the paired-cuvette preparation
scope.condition: donor optically coupled to (a) a live conspecific receiver, (b) a heat-killed receiver at identical turbidity and scattering, (c) medium only, (d) an opaque shutter - order randomised, operator blind, with donor oxygen consumption and temperature logged continuously
scope.comparator: condition (d), the opaque-shutter arm, at matched donor metabolic rate
scope.outcome: donor photon count rate per unit oxygen consumed, per 50 nm band

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: rho departs from 1 by more than 25 percent in a blinded, metabolic-rate-matched comparison - demonstrating sender-side, receiver-contingent regulation of emission and falsifying this hypothesis.
hypothesis.estimand: rho = [donor photons per unit O2 consumed, live receiver optically coupled] / [donor photons per unit O2 consumed, opaque shutter]. Claim: rho within [0.80, 1.25].

rationale.step: The seed question is whether UPE is a byproduct of metabolism or carries an informational or functional role.

A trait counts as a signal only if its production is contingent on the communicative context; a trait whose production is fully accounted for by the sender's own metabolic state is a cue. Receiver-contingency of emission, measured at matched metabolic rate, is therefore the sharpest emitter-side operationalisation of 'signal', and it is logically independent of whether any receiver effect exists - it can be decided even if every receiver-side claim in the field is false.

Existing distant-cellular-interaction preparations report mutual or bidirectional effects and growth correlation between coupled populations, which - if the reports are real - entails that donors are not passive lamps and makes receiver-contingent emission a live possibility rather than an idle one.

UPE tracks metabolic and oxidative rate, and has been reported to co-vary with cerebral blood flow and energy metabolism, so any comparison that does not hold metabolic rate fixed is confounded at the outset - which is why simultaneous respirometry is load-bearing here rather than decorative.

The same 'beyond global metabolic rate' structure is already what the field demands of neural UPE claims, where photon activity has been imaged in situ during stimulation without the metabolic covariate being separated out.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Two thermostatted chambers joined by a computer-controlled quartz shutter, each with its own photon-counting PMT and in-line optical oxygen sensor. The donor chamber's emission is recorded continuously in 50 nm bands while the receiver chamber is cycled, in randomised blocks, through live receiver, heat-killed receiver at matched turbidity, medium only, and shutter closed. Turbidity and scattering are matched optically before the run so back-scatter into the donor PMT is identical across arms. All analysis is on photons per unit O2 consumed; the analyst is blind to arm labels. Pre-register the 25 percent decision band and the metabolic-matching tolerance. Because a positive result here is the single cheapest route to 'signal', it should be run in at least two labs with a shipped calibration standard.
hypothesis.required_instrument: dual-channel photon-counting PMT (300-650 nm) with computer-controlled quartz shutter and transmission-matched windows; thermostatted dark chambers; in-line optical O2 sensors on both chambers
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: Imports the signal-versus-cue criterion from communication theory and turns it into a measurement on the emitter. Nothing on the register tests whether the emitter modulates output as a function of receiver presence; H6 asks the 'beyond metabolic rate' question of neural activity, and nobody asks it of the social or optical context. It is also the only route on this list by which the functional-role question could be settled affirmatively without any receiver-side photon budget being solved.

members.statement: Reported optical-only donor-to-receiver effects survive removal of the receiver's candidate photoacceptors - no single chromophore knockout or pharmacological block abolishes them - which means those effects are not photochemical.

hypothesis.statement: Reported optical-only donor-to-receiver effects survive removal of the receiver's candidate photoacceptors - no single chromophore knockout or pharmacological block abolishes them - which means those effects are not photochemical.

scope.population: genetically tractable receivers: Arabidopsis thaliana cry1 cry2 double mutants and phot1 phot2 mutants; human adipose-derived stem cells with TRPV1 blocked by capsazepine or with CRY1/CRY2 knocked down
scope.condition: receiver exposed across a quartz (200 nm cut-on) window to a proliferating conspecific or same-line donor whose in-band emission is monitored continuously by a calibrated PMT
scope.comparator: isogenic wild-type receiver run in the same session, plus a long-pass optical block that removes the candidate chromophore's absorption band while leaving all non-optical coupling intact
scope.outcome: receiver proliferation index (EdU incorporation) or germination and growth rate, with intracellular Ca2+ and ROS as pathway readouts

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: A specific photoacceptor removal cuts the effect by 80 percent or more while the wild-type effect is intact in the same session - identifying a molecular receiver and falsifying this hypothesis.
hypothesis.estimand: f = (effect size in the photoacceptor-deficient receiver) / (effect size in the isogenic wild type), same session, blinded. Claim: f >= 0.8 for every candidate tested.

rationale.step: Light-sensitive proteins and light-responsive processes are now localised to many non-ocular cell types and tissues, so a receiver molecule is available in principle and the knockout panel is not a strawman.

A fully characterised receiver pathway already exists for blue and green light in human adipose-derived stem cells - TRPV1 activation, raised intracellular Ca2+ and ROS, proliferation inhibited, all abolished by capsazepine and by N-acetylcysteine - which supplies both the positive control and the dose scale, since it operates at 3 J cm^-2.

Per-cell photon interception: a mammalian cell footprint is about 10 um x 10 um = 1e-6 cm^2. At a generous 1e4 photons cm^-2 s^-1 the cell intercepts 1e-2 photons s^-1, about 864 per 24 h. At the more typical 10-100 photons cm^-2 s^-1 it intercepts 1e-5 to 1e-4 photons s^-1, i.e. about 0.9 to 8.6 photons per cell per day. With an in-band chromophore absorbing of order 1 percent of incident photons, the receiver absorbs about 0.01-0.1 photons per cell per day.

A 24 h proliferation change therefore requires a phenotypic response from fewer than one absorbed photon per cell - most responding cells would have absorbed nothing at all. This is why photoacceptor necessity is the decisive test and not merely a mechanistic nicety: a genuinely photochemical effect must funnel through some absorber, and no absorber can be bypassed.

The most sensitive photodetector biology is known to build, the vertebrate rod, was tested against exactly this budget: absolutely calibrated measurement of retinal and eyecup emission found biophoton intensity at least 100-fold too low to account even for the rods' own discrete dark noise, against a measured rhodopsin activation rate constant of 1.2e-11 s^-1 in frog and 7.6e-11 s^-1 in sterlet.

Rod sensitivity rests on a large transduction cascade gain - one activated metarhodopsin activating hundreds of transducins, each driving further amplification - which non-specialised receivers do not possess, so a non-specialised cell would have to beat the best specialised detector in biology to close the gap.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Dual-chamber quartz-windowed optical coupler with a calibrated photon-counting PMT tapping the donor output continuously (solar-blind channel 200-320 nm, bialkali channel 300-650 nm), so the delivered budget is recorded rather than assumed. Each session runs wild-type and photoacceptor-deficient receivers side by side against the same donor, with arm assignment blinded. Positive control: the same receivers exposed to 3 J cm^-2 of 415 nm or 540 nm light, where the TRPV1/Ca2+/ROS pathway is known to respond and the knockout or capsazepine block must abolish the response - this validates the knockout before the UPE arm is interpreted. Panel: cry1 cry2, phot1 phot2, OPN3 knockdown, TRPV1 block, and a flavin-depletion arm. Pre-register f = 0.8 as the decision boundary.
hypothesis.required_instrument: dual-chamber quartz-windowed optical coupler; photon-counting PMT with a solar-blind channel (200-320 nm) and a bialkali channel (300-650 nm) monitoring donor output in absolute units; standard EdU, Fura-2/GCaMP and ROS imaging on the receiver
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: Register H5 and H1 assume without test that the receiver possesses a photoacceptor with adequate absorption cross-section. This exposes that assumption and converts it into a molecular-necessity experiment with a built-in validated positive control, and attaches to it a per-cell absorbed-photon budget - about 0.01-0.1 absorbed photons per cell per day - that the register never computes.

members.statement: Absolutely calibrated solar-blind photon counting of the 200-320 nm band from densely proliferating cultures behind an MgF2 window will find an emission rate below 1 photon cm^-2 s^-1 at the window, orders of magnitude too low for any mitogenetic-band mechanism.

hypothesis.statement: Absolutely calibrated solar-blind photon counting of the 200-320 nm band from densely proliferating cultures behind an MgF2 window will find an emission rate below 1 photon cm^-2 s^-1 at the window, orders of magnitude too low for any mitogenetic-band mechanism.

scope.population: densely proliferating Saccharomyces cerevisiae and one proliferating mammalian line, prepared as thin films or with a sub-millimetre aqueous path behind MgF2 or synthetic-silica windows
scope.condition: dark-adapted, thermostatted, solar-blind photon counting in 20 nm bins from 200 to 320 nm, with a second bialkali channel recording 300-650 nm simultaneously
scope.comparator: heat-killed sample at matched turbidity; medium-only blank; instrument dark count in the same band; whole-chain traceable calibration with a deuterium lamp and vacuum-UV monochromator including window and water path
scope.outcome: absolute photon rate in photons cm^-2 s^-1 at the sample window, per 20 nm bin from 200 to 320 nm

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The 200-320 nm rate is 100 photons cm^-2 s^-1 or more above blank - falsifying this hypothesis and handing the mitogenetic-band mechanism the photon budget it has never had.
hypothesis.estimand: N_UV = absolute emission rate integrated over 200-320 nm, in photons cm^-2 s^-1 at the sample window, blank-subtracted. Claim: N_UV < 1.

rationale.step: Gurwitsch-type mitogenetic mechanisms require emission in the deep UV (190-250 nm), and the modern open-quantum-systems revival of the onion experiment explicitly assumes UV intensities of 10 to 1e4 photons s^-1 cm^-2 from active cells as the input to its resonance model.

The field's own signal-to-noise review states that the Gurwitsch 190-250 nm claim is highly controversial and that there is little modern evidence even for the longer 280-390 nm UV band in biological photon emission.

Modern reviews quote UPE as spanning roughly 260-800 nm (some as wide as 200-1300 nm) at a few to a few hundred photons cm^-2 s^-1 total, but the UV share is never separately budgeted in absolute units - the total is reported and the band composition is inferred from cut-on filters.

The dedicated review of the mitogenetic controversy concludes that the UV fraction of UPE should be regarded as real while its biological effects remain hard to reproduce - the exact asymmetry that an absolute, band-resolved UV budget would resolve in one measurement.

Water absorbs strongly below about 200 nm and borosilicate cuts off below about 340 nm, while the widely used bialkali PMTs and EMCCD/LCTF spectrometers are optimised for 400-700 nm and cannot separate a deep-UV component from visible dark count. So nearly every UPE instrument in the corpus is structurally blind to the mitogenetic band; MgF2 or synthetic silica plus a CsI or CsTe solar-blind photocathode is the minimum chain that can measure it, and the same chain measures its own dark count inside the band of interest.

Fels reported different outcomes across glass (transmitting above about 340 nm) versus quartz (transmitting from about 150 nm) barriers, and the adipose-stem-cell replication used a UV-filter tube versus a quartz tube - so the entire glass-versus-quartz design logic in this literature presupposes a deep-UV budget that has never been measured in absolute units.
The field names absolutely calibrated photon budgets as the criterion that would settle the functional-role question, and the mitogenetic band is where that criterion has never been applied.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Assemble a vacuum-UV-capable dark chamber: sample in a thin-film or sub-millimetre-path holder behind an MgF2 window, viewed by a solar-blind photon-counting PMT (CsI or CsTe photocathode) through a stepped set of 20 nm bandpass filters covering 200-320 nm, with a second bialkali channel on 300-650 nm for simultaneous total-UPE reference. Calibrate the entire chain end to end - window, filters, water path, photocathode - against a deuterium lamp through a vacuum-UV monochromator, with the transfer standard shipped between the participating labs. Run live culture, heat-killed matched-turbidity control, medium-only blank and closed-shutter dark count in randomised blocks, blinded, integrating long enough that the blank-subtracted 1 photon cm^-2 s^-1 boundary is resolved with pre-registered power. Report N_UV in absolute units per bin, whichever way it falls.
hypothesis.required_instrument: solar-blind photon-counting PMT (CsI or CsTe photocathode, 160-320 nm) or UV SiPM behind MgF2 / synthetic-silica windows with 20 nm bandpass set; deuterium lamp plus vacuum-UV monochromator for traceable end-to-end calibration; second bialkali photon-counting channel, 300-650 nm
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: Register H11 asks whether the spectral distribution carries state information beyond total intensity. Nobody on the register asks for an absolute, band-resolved budget in the one band the mitogenetic mechanism actually needs, measured with a detector that is blind to the visible so the dark count cannot masquerade as signal. N_UV is a single number that decides whether H1 is physically possible at all, and it also retro-validates or invalidates the glass-versus-quartz contrast on which the whole distant-cellular-interaction design tradition rests.

members.statement: In clonally split Paramecium caudatum populations exposed for 48 hours in darkness, the growth effect of a live emitter population across a sealed quartz optical path will be reproduced within a preregistered 20% equivalence margin by photon-for-photon replay of its absolutely calibrated 300–750 nm emission, while an opaque shutter will abolish the effect.

hypothesis.statement: In clonally split Paramecium caudatum populations exposed for 48 hours in darkness, the growth effect of a live emitter population across a sealed quartz optical path will be reproduced within a preregistered 20% equivalence margin by photon-for-photon replay of its absolutely calibrated 300–750 nm emission, while an opaque shutter will abolish the effect.

scope.population: Clonal P. caudatum receiver populations started at 5 cells/mL.
scope.condition: Forty-eight-hour exposure in darkness across double-sealed quartz compartments with independent gas spaces, tested by at least three blinded laboratories.
scope.comparator: Live-emitter coupling, opaque-shutter coupling, emitter-free sham, and attenuated multi-LED replay matched to the live emitter's spectrum and receiver-plane photon flux.
scope.outcome: Receiver population growth, expressed as log cell-number change from 0 to 48 hours.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The live-emitter contrast is absent, survives the opaque shutter, or is not equivalent within ±20% to the photon-matched replay contrast.
hypothesis.estimand: The ratio of the replay-versus-sham growth contrast to the live-emitter-versus-shutter growth contrast, with equivalence bounds 0.80–1.20, together with the shutter residual contrast.

rationale.step: P. caudatum populations separated by glass or quartz in darkness were reported to alter neighboring populations' division and energy uptake.

A distant proliferation effect in adipose-derived stem cells was instead attributed to volatile signaling after optical-container controls reduced the effect, making independent gas isolation a load-bearing control.
High-albedo photon concentration has detected growth-associated yeast emission, and the same work identifies missing absolute photon reporting as a major measurement gap.

For each wavelength bin, the receiver dose is computed as N_receiver = integral[Phi_emitter(lambda,t) × T_window(lambda) × G_geometry(lambda) dt d(lambda)]; matching this quantity in replay makes equality of the two biological contrasts a direct photon-budget closure test.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Pre-register and distribute identical clonal cultures and coded exposure cartridges to three laboratories. Randomize receivers among live-emitter, opaque-shutter, sham, and replay arms. Quantify sister emitter cultures continuously, propagate measured window transmission and geometry to receiver-plane photon dose, and replay the resulting spectrum and time course from a calibrated attenuated LED array. Automated image cytometry performs blinded 0- and 48-hour cell counts.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Absolutely calibrated cooled photon-counting PMT or silicon-SPAD spectrometer covering 300–750 nm, high-albedo integrating cavity, calibrated quartz transmission standards, attenuated multiwavelength LED replay source, and automated bright-field cell counter.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This advances beyond H5 by requiring photon-for-photon causal substitution: natural emitters must be replaceable by an artificial source at the measured receiver dose, not merely associated with an opaque-versus-transparent difference.

members.statement: For optically coupled P. caudatum, the dose-normalized receiver-growth effects in four spectral bands will form the same action-spectrum ranking under live-emitter coupling and synthetic photon replay, with Spearman rho at least 0.8 and at least one familywise-error-controlled nonzero band effect.

hypothesis.statement: For optically coupled P. caudatum, the dose-normalized receiver-growth effects in four spectral bands will form the same action-spectrum ranking under live-emitter coupling and synthetic photon replay, with Spearman rho at least 0.8 and at least one familywise-error-controlled nonzero band effect.

scope.population: Clonal P. caudatum emitter and receiver populations.
scope.condition: Forty-eight-hour dark exposure through sealed quartz paths partitioned into 260–340, 340–450, 450–600, and 600–750 nm bands.
scope.comparator: Equal receiver-plane photon counts delivered by filtered live emitters versus narrowband synthetic replay, with opaque and zero-photon controls.
scope.outcome: Dose-normalized difference in receiver log growth for each spectral band.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: No band has a corrected nonzero effect, or the live-emitter and replay action spectra have Spearman rho below 0.8.
hypothesis.estimand: The four-band vector of growth contrast per received photon and its Spearman correlation between natural and replay exposures.

rationale.step: Glass and quartz separators produced different P. caudatum effects, and the original interpretation invoked at least two frequency regions.

Historical claims place mitogenetic emission in the ultraviolet, but modern evidence for even 280–390 nm emission was judged limited, so the ultraviolet contribution requires direct measurement rather than inference from window material.
A proposed framework for light-based cellular interaction explicitly requires both a modulated optical signal and molecular perception by the receiver.

Equalizing N_receiver across bands removes total photon count as the explanation; correlation of the dose-normalized natural and replay effect vectors then tests whether wavelength-specific photon absorption predicts the receiver response.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Measure the live-emitter spectrum and filter transmission in the complete exposure cartridge, then expose randomized receivers through one band at a time. In a second factorial arm, use narrowband LEDs attenuated to the same receiver-plane photon count. Estimate band-specific growth contrasts with a preregistered hierarchical model and compare the two action-spectrum vectors.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Absolutely calibrated solar-blind UV PMT for 260–400 nm plus a cooled red-sensitive photon-counting PMT or EMCCD spectrometer for 340–750 nm, monochromator or interference-filter wheel, and attenuated UV/visible LED array.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This replaces the register's broad spectral-information and photon-causality claims with a receiver action-spectrum identity test that can distinguish photons from a window-material artifact.

members.statement: At identical total photon count and spectrum, replaying the measured one-second-scale temporal order of P. caudatum UPE will change receiver growth relative to replaying a within-10-minute-block permutation of the same photon sequence.

hypothesis.statement: At identical total photon count and spectrum, replaying the measured one-second-scale temporal order of P. caudatum UPE will change receiver growth relative to replaying a within-10-minute-block permutation of the same photon sequence.

scope.population: Clonal P. caudatum receivers started at 5 cells/mL and emitter populations measured in the same growth phase.
scope.condition: Forty-eight-hour dark exposure to multi-band LED replay generated from time-tagged natural-emission records.
scope.comparator: Original-order replay versus block-permuted replay, with photon count in every spectral channel and every 10-minute block held exactly constant.
scope.outcome: Difference in receiver log growth at 48 hours.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The original-order and temporally permuted replays produce the same receiver growth within a preregistered ±5% equivalence margin.
hypothesis.estimand: The original-minus-permuted difference in 48-hour log growth, with total and band-specific delivered photon counts constrained to equality.

rationale.step: Time-series analysis of astrocyte and glioblastoma UPE found anomalous diffusion and long-range memory, showing that biological emission can contain measurable temporal structure beyond mean intensity.
The light-communication framework requires secondary modulation of an optical signal by emitter cells.

Human dental-pulp stem-cell responses to 810 nm photobiomodulation depended on pulse frequency, demonstrating at a higher optical dose that cellular outcome can depend on temporal delivery rather than energy alone.

Because permutation preserves sum_t N(lambda,t) separately for each wavelength channel and 10-minute block, a nonzero outcome contrast is attributable to sub-block temporal ordering rather than photon dose, spectrum, or slow drift.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Record emitter photons with two independent time-tagging detector channels to reject detector bursts, construct original and block-permuted multi-band replay files, and expose coded receiver cultures using the same LED hardware. Verify equality of delivered counts with an independent monitor detector and score growth blindly.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Dual time-correlated single-photon-counting PMTs or SPADs covering 300–750 nm with one-second or finer time tags, spectrally multiplexed attenuated LED replay, and calibrated monitor photodetector.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This advances beyond H11 by asking whether temporal UPE structure is causally decoded by a receiver, rather than merely carrying correlational information about the emitter.

members.statement: The reported suppression of 5-cells/mL P. caudatum indicator growth by 50–300-cells/mL neighbors is an analog photon-dose response whose between-density variation is fully explained by absolutely measured 300–750 nm receiver fluence, with no residual emitter-density effect.

hypothesis.statement: The reported suppression of 5-cells/mL P. caudatum indicator growth by 50–300-cells/mL neighbors is an analog photon-dose response whose between-density variation is fully explained by absolutely measured 300–750 nm receiver fluence, with no residual emitter-density effect.

scope.population: P. caudatum indicators started at 5 cells/mL, paired with emitters started at 50, 100, 200, or 300 cells/mL.
scope.condition: Forty-eight-hour exposure in darkness through sealed optical paths and a crossed series of calibrated neutral-density attenuations.
scope.comparator: Different emitter densities adjusted to overlapping receiver-plane photon doses, plus opaque, sham, and synthetic-replay controls.
scope.outcome: Indicator log growth and its dose-response relationship to received photon fluence.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: Growth suppression is not monotonic with measured photon fluence, or emitter density improves held-out prediction after photon dose is included.
hypothesis.estimand: The cross-validated dose-response function f(N_receiver) and the incremental held-out log-likelihood contributed by emitter-density labels after f(N_receiver), with less than two AIC-equivalent units treated as no residual contribution.

rationale.step: Indicators started at 5 cells/mL reportedly grew less when surrounded by 50, 100, 200, or 300 cells/mL, and graphite shielding removed the neighbor effect.
Weak cellular emission and unfavorable signal-to-noise ratio have been identified as physical obstacles to light-based cell communication.
A high-albedo cavity can recover a large fraction of photons from an extended biological volume, enabling absolute flux estimation at intensities relevant to growing cell populations.

Crossing four densities with several transmissions creates overlapping doses; fitting growth = alpha + f(N_receiver) + batch and then testing density terms separates photon-dose sufficiency from density-linked non-optical confounding.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Repeat the published 5-versus-50/100/200/300-cells/mL design using double-sealed cartridges. Cross density with neutral-density filters chosen to make different densities deliver overlapping photon fluences. Measure transmitted photons continuously in matched cartridges, reproduce selected doses synthetically, and compare dose-only and dose-plus-density models by preregistered leave-batch-out validation.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Absolutely calibrated photon-counting PMT or SPAD system covering 300–750 nm, high-albedo integrating cavity, calibrated neutral-density filters, monitor detector, and automated cell-count imaging.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This turns the reported population-density effect into a quantitative analog-quorum hypothesis and tests whether received photon number is sufficient, a mechanism not specified by H5.

members.statement: After equalizing total 300–750 nm photon count, replay of the joint spectral-temporal UPE template from a 300-cells/mL P. caudatum population will suppress growth of 5-cells/mL receivers by at least 10% more than replay of the template from a 50-cells/mL population.

hypothesis.statement: After equalizing total 300–750 nm photon count, replay of the joint spectral-temporal UPE template from a 300-cells/mL P. caudatum population will suppress growth of 5-cells/mL receivers by at least 10% more than replay of the template from a 50-cells/mL population.

scope.population: Clonal P. caudatum receivers started at 5 cells/mL.
scope.condition: Forty-eight-hour dark exposure to photon replays derived from emitters started at 50 or 300 cells/mL.
scope.comparator: Low-density and high-density emitter templates normalized to identical integrated receiver-plane photon count, plus spectrally flattened and temporally shuffled versions.
scope.outcome: Percent difference in receiver population growth at 48 hours.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The normalized high-density template suppresses growth by less than 10% relative to the normalized low-density template, or the difference disappears once photon count is equalized.
hypothesis.estimand: One minus the ratio of 48-hour receiver growth under the normalized 300-cells/mL template to growth under the normalized 50-cells/mL template.

rationale.step: P. caudatum indicator growth reportedly decreased as neighboring population density increased from 50 to 300 cells/mL.
P. caudatum effects were reported to vary in sign with cell number and separator material, which is compatible with a structured cue rather than a universally stimulatory photon dose.
Biological UPE time series can contain long-memory dynamics, while a theoretical communication framework identifies emitter modulation as a required component of information transfer.

Normalizing both templates so that sum_lambda,t N_50(lambda,t) equals sum_lambda,t N_300(lambda,t) removes integrated intensity; a remaining growth difference measures information in the spectral-temporal distribution.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Acquire replicated, time-resolved spectra from 50- and 300-cells/mL emitters, normalize templates to the same receiver-plane photon total, and replay them to blinded 5-cells/mL receivers. Factorially flatten spectrum or shuffle time to determine which component carries any density-dependent effect.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Time-tagged photon-counting spectrometer covering 300–750 nm, calibrated multiwavelength LED or monochromator replay system capable of single-photon-level attenuation, and automated cell counter.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This is the explicit pattern-coded rival to Q3-4's intensity-only quorum model and tests whether equal numbers of photons convey different density messages.

members.statement: A photon-matched P. caudatum growth signal will retain at least half of its dark-condition effect when superposed on spectrally matched Poisson background light delivering ten times the signal photon count, indicating receiver-side filtering rather than dependence on an unrealistically noise-free channel.

hypothesis.statement: A photon-matched P. caudatum growth signal will retain at least half of its dark-condition effect when superposed on spectrally matched Poisson background light delivering ten times the signal photon count, indicating receiver-side filtering rather than dependence on an unrealistically noise-free channel.

scope.population: Clonal P. caudatum receivers started at 5 cells/mL.
scope.condition: Forty-eight-hour replay exposure under backgrounds of 0, 1, 10, and 100 times the measured UPE photon count.
scope.comparator: Identical UPE replay with no background, spectrally matched Poisson background, temporally structured background, and background-only controls.
scope.outcome: Receiver growth contrast attributable to the fixed UPE replay at each background level.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: At tenfold background, the replay-attributable growth contrast is less than 50% of its dark-condition value or is statistically indistinguishable from zero.
hypothesis.estimand: The ratio of the replay-versus-background-only growth contrast at tenfold background to the replay-versus-sham contrast in darkness.

rationale.step: The principal P. caudatum optical-coupling report performed mutual exposure under darkness.
A quantitative feasibility analysis concluded that weak emission and unfavorable ambient signal-to-noise ratio are major obstacles to cellular light communication.

For each condition, signal-to-background ratio is computed as SBR = N_signal/N_background after weighting both spectra by measured window transmission; fixing N_signal while increasing N_background directly estimates the receiver's noise-tolerance curve.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: First establish a photon-matched replay effect in darkness. Repeat the coded exposure with independently generated Poisson and structured backgrounds at defined multiples of the signal dose, continuously verify both components with a monitor detector, and estimate the preregistered signal-by-background interaction across laboratories.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Absolutely calibrated photon-counting PMT or SPAD covering 300–750 nm, two independently driven attenuated multiwavelength LED sources for signal and background, optical combiner, and monitor spectrometer.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This exposes the hidden noise-free-channel assumption in darkness-only coupling studies and supplies a quantitative criterion for whether a laboratory photon effect could function outside exceptional darkness.

members.statement: Under properly background-free dark conditions, the transmission- and detector-weighted fraction of extracranially detected photons that originate below the skull is below 5% for any photomultiplier-based head measurement, so head UPE recorded with bialkali/multialkali PMTs is scalp-dominated rather than brain-dominated.

hypothesis.statement: Under properly background-free dark conditions, the transmission- and detector-weighted fraction of extracranially detected photons that originate below the skull is below 5% for any photomultiplier-based head measurement, so head UPE recorded with bialkali/multialkali PMTs is scalp-dominated rather than brain-dominated.

scope.population: Healthy adults, n>=20, stratified by Fitzpatrick skin type and including a shaved-scalp/bald stratum; plus a tissue-equivalent head phantom containing a calibrated sub-skull emitter of known spectrum and rate.
scope.condition: >=4 h continuous dark adaptation in a light-tight, temperature-controlled chamber; simultaneous two-band photon counting through one shared collection optic over occipital and temporal scalp; per-subject scalp+skull transmission T(lambda) measured 450-900 nm on the same head.
scope.comparator: Matched non-cranial skin site (volar forearm) on the same subject at matched skin temperature and cutaneous perfusion, measured in the same session with the same optic; plus the phantom arm in which the sub-skull source rate is known.
scope.outcome: Two-band count ratio R = N(700-900 nm)/N(400-600 nm) at head vs skin site, and the inferred sub-skull-origin fraction beta obtained by fitting head counts with measured T(lambda) and detector response Q(lambda).

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: beta has a 95% CI whose lower bound exceeds 0.05, i.e. the head shows a long-wavelength excess over matched skin that a scalp-only emission model with the measured T(lambda) and Q(lambda) cannot reproduce; the hypothesis is then dead and extracranial brain detection is real at PMT sensitivity.
hypothesis.estimand: beta = inferred sub-skull-origin fraction of the head count rate, with 95% CI; pre-registered decision threshold beta < 0.05. Secondary estimand: R_head - R_forearm after temperature and perfusion adjustment.

rationale.step: Salari et al. measured head UPE under properly dark conditions at 40 counts/s against a 22 counts/s dark rate (net 18 counts/s, flux approx. 41 photons cm^-2 s^-1) and argue that the far larger signals in the extracranial 'brain UPE' literature are explained by background light contamination; they further argue that <600 nm is strongly attenuated by scalp and skull while longer wavelengths fall largely outside effective PMT sensitivity.

The extracranial brain-UPE program is being standardised into a measurement modality (photoencephalography), with a published measurement/analysis protocol and a methodological-and-ethical framing paper, so the provenance question is load-bearing for a whole emerging readout rather than for one disputed dataset.

Direct measurements on brain tissue place the emission mostly below 700 nm: hypoxic rat brain chemiluminescence spectra show peaks at 480, 520-530, 570, 620-640 and 680-700 nm; rat hippocampal slices emit at the order of 1e-19 W/mm2 detected with a silicon avalanche photodiode; and in vivo rat brain imaging detects emission in the visible band.

Human skin is itself a strong and spectrally resolvable UPE source across roughly 400-700 nm, measurable with EMCCD plus liquid-crystal tunable filter, with the 500-600 nm region attributed in part to melanin; this is the competing scalp source that any head measurement must exclude.

Define the detection-efficiency integral eta = INT E(lambda) T(lambda) Q(lambda) d(lambda) / INT E(lambda) d(lambda), where E is the source emission spectrum, T the scalp+skull transmission and Q the detector spectral response. From the cited spectra, E for brain tissue is concentrated at 480-700 nm; T is smallest exactly over that interval and rises toward the near infrared; Q for bialkali/multialkali photocathodes falls steeply beyond about 650 nm. The product is therefore suppressed in both halves of the spectrum, so eta for a sub-skull source is smaller than eta for a scalp source (where T is approximately 1 for the outermost emitting layer) by orders of magnitude. Total head intensity therefore cannot discriminate the two sources, whereas the two-band ratio R can, because a sub-skull source is filtered by T(lambda) and a scalp source is not. This is the photon-budget calculation the field says must precede data collection.

The seed brief states that the field's own settlement criteria for this question are tissue-optics-informed detection in bands that actually transmit, photon-budget modelling before data collection, and Salari-style artifact controls; eta and beta are those criteria written as numbers.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Build a two-channel head photon counter sharing one collection optic and one aperture, one channel filtered 400-600 nm and one 700-900 nm, inside a light-tight chamber with continuously logged dark rate. For each subject: (1) log ambient light dose for 24 h before the session; (2) dark-adapt >=4 h; (3) record head and volar-forearm sites in counterbalanced order with skin thermography and laser-Doppler perfusion recorded at the detector footprint; (4) measure that subject's scalp+skull transmission 450-900 nm in situ with a calibrated low-power source and a reference detector. Fit the head two-band counts with a two-compartment model (scalp layer, sub-skull layer) using the measured T(lambda) and the manufacturer-plus-calibration Q(lambda) to recover beta. Validate the whole inference chain on the phantom, where the sub-skull emitter rate is known and beta has a ground truth. Report eta for the instrument as a mandatory instrument specification.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Two matched photon-counting channels on one collection optic in a light-tight, temperature-stabilised chamber: (a) cooled bialkali/multialkali PMT with 400-600 nm bandpass; (b) cooled GaAs- or InGaAsP-photocathode PMT, or cooled Si single-photon avalanche diode, with 700-900 nm bandpass. Plus: NIST-traceable radiance standard for absolute calibration; in-situ transmission rig (calibrated source + reference detector) covering 450-900 nm; skin thermography and laser-Doppler perfusion monitoring; 24 h wearable ambient-light dosimeter.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: The register carries H6 (intracranial UPE vs neural activity, invasive) and H12 (mental states vs surface UPE) but contains no provenance claim and no estimand for where extracranially detected photons come from. This converts the field's qualitative worry into two pre-registerable numbers, eta (an instrument specification any future head study must state) and beta (a per-subject source-attribution fraction), and it makes a two-band ratio against a matched non-cranial skin site, not total intensity, the discriminating observable.

members.statement: In acute mouse coronal brain slices, at least half of the glutamate-evoked ultraweak photon emission increment survives complete action-potential blockade with tetrodotoxin while mitochondrial electron-transport inhibition abolishes it, establishing that evoked 'brain biophotonic activity' is a redox/metabolic readout rather than a spike-borne signalling event.

hypothesis.statement: In acute mouse coronal brain slices, at least half of the glutamate-evoked ultraweak photon emission increment survives complete action-potential blockade with tetrodotoxin while mitochondrial electron-transport inhibition abolishes it, establishing that evoked 'brain biophotonic activity' is a redox/metabolic readout rather than a spike-borne signalling event.

scope.population: Acute 400 um coronal brain slices from adult C57BL/6 mice, n>=12 slices per arm from >=6 animals, slices randomised across arms and imaged one per chamber run.
scope.condition: 50 mM glutamate perfusion for >=90 min under four arms: (i) control aCSF; (ii) 1 uM TTX with spike blockade verified by a paired field-potential electrode; (iii) sodium azide plus oxygen-glucose deprivation; (iv) TTX plus azide/OGD.
scope.comparator: Vehicle-perfused slices from the same animals, and each slice's own 30 min pre-glutamate baseline.
scope.outcome: Integrated photon counts over 400-900 nm across the 90-200 min plateau, normalised to that slice's pre-glutamate baseline; paired per-slice TBARS/malondialdehyde and total thiol assays on the same tissue.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: TTX removes more than half of the glutamate-evoked increment (upper 95% bound of the preserved fraction f falls below 0.5) while metabolic substrate is held constant, which would make the evoked emission spike-dependent and would license reading brain UPE as an activity/communication signal rather than an oxidation readout.
hypothesis.estimand: f = (evoked increment under 1 uM TTX) / (evoked increment under control aCSF), with 95% CI; claim: lower CI bound of f >= 0.5, with the azide/OGD arm increment CI including 0. Secondary: partial R2 of a spike-rate regressor after per-slice lipid-peroxidation markers are entered first.

rationale.step: Tang and Dai report that the glutamate-evoked biophotonic increase in mouse brain slices is significantly blocked by oxygen-glucose deprivation together with a cytochrome c oxidase inhibitor (sodium azide), but only partly by an action-potential inhibitor (TTX), by an anaesthetic (procaine), or by removal of intracellular and extracellular Ca2+.

The competing result the estimand must adjudicate: in rat hippocampal slices, potassium depolarisation increased and TTX decreased ultraweak biochemiluminescence, which is the strongest existing case for spike-linked brain emission.

Activity-dependent neural tissue oxidation has been reported to emit intrinsic ultraweak photons, which ties evoked brain emission to oxidation rather than to spiking as such; in vivo rat brain UPE likewise correlates with cerebral energy metabolism and oxidative stress.

In isolated rat brains, ketamine increased UPE together with lipid peroxidation and antioxidant enzyme activity while reducing thiols, whereas thiopental decreased UPE, oxidative markers and enzyme activity while increasing thiols; UPE correlated negatively with thiol level and positively with oxidative markers.

Both anaesthetics abolish responsiveness, yet they move UPE in opposite directions, so any model in which whole-brain UPE intensity is a monotone function of neural activity or of consciousness is already falsified at the whole-organ level; the surviving candidate is that UPE tracks oxidative load.
