Dividing the absolute emission rate by an independently assayed J cancels the biological driver and leaves Phi_UPE, which is a property of the chemistry alone; therefore any residual between-laboratory spread in Phi_UPE beyond the stated assay uncertainty is, by construction, instrumental. A factor-of-three tolerance is the right threshold because it is smaller than the ~1.4-decade spread that unreported g, eta_bar and T can generate but larger than the assay's own reproducibility.

The claim is currently untestable in the literature because emission is not reported in absolute units: reported spontaneous UPE spans 1-1000 and 10-10^3 photons s-1 cm-2 across sources with no shared conversion, and some current measurement reports give only relative light units.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: In each of >=3 laboratories with different detector classes, run a Fenton dose series on a common S. cerevisiae strain at fixed OD in defined medium, measuring absolute photon emission (350-700 nm, converted to photons s-1 into 4 pi using measured eta(lambda), collection solid angle and transmission) while assaying H2O2 consumption on parallel aliquots by a standard peroxide assay, plus the cell-free medium control at each dose. Compute the regression slope in absolute units - that slope is Phi_UPE. Independently, measure the same culture's spontaneous emission and its baseline ROS flux, and test whether Phi_UPE * J predicts the observed spontaneous rate within 10x. Repeat the numerator/denominator pairing in Chlamydomonas with linoleic acid and TBARS. Refutation: between-laboratory spread of Phi_UPE > 1 decade, or prediction error > 10x.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Cooled PMT photon counter (350-700 nm) with in-house measured eta(lambda) and dark rate, optionally coupled to a high-albedo Ulbricht cavity for 4 pi collection; cross-check arm: EMCCD operated as a binary photon-counter array (400-900 nm); plus a standard spectrophotometric/fluorimetric peroxide and TBARS assay.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: H4a claims that known oxidative pathways account for the dominant fraction of spontaneous UPE intensity, but 'dominant fraction' has never been given a number because emission is not reported in absolute units. This sharpens H4a into a closed photon budget with an explicit quantity (photons per oxidant molecule), an explicit cell-free chemiexcitation baseline, and a factor-of-ten prediction test - the decisive measurable form the register does not contain, and one whose failure would be informative in the opposite direction from H4a's current framing.

members.statement: For mechanically wounded seven-week-old Arabidopsis thaliana, independently calibrated PMT and EMCCD measurements of the 400–870 nm photon-emission-rate-density integral over the first 30 minutes after incision will be equivalent within ±15%.

hypothesis.statement: For mechanically wounded seven-week-old Arabidopsis thaliana, independently calibrated PMT and EMCCD measurements of the 400–870 nm photon-emission-rate-density integral over the first 30 minutes after incision will be equivalent within ±15%.

scope.population: Seven-week-old Arabidopsis thaliana plants, with at least 30 plants per detector comparison
scope.condition: Two-hour dark adaptation followed by a standardized sharp leaf incision and simultaneous 30-minute acquisition
scope.comparator: A red-sensitive photon-counting PMT versus a back-illuminated EMCCD viewing the same leaf through a calibrated beam splitter
scope.outcome: Background-subtracted 400–870 nm photon emission per second per square centimetre, integrated over 30 minutes

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The 90% confidence interval for the PMT-to-EMCCD mean emission-density ratio is not wholly contained within 0.85–1.15.
hypothesis.estimand: Ratio of geometric-mean calibrated 30-minute emission-density integrals from the PMT and EMCCD.

rationale.step: The seed brief identifies the absence of absolute photon units and direct instrument comparability as the metrology hole.
Standardized incision of seven-week-old Arabidopsis produces measurable UPE extending through 400–870 nm, with a dominant 700–750 nm contribution.

A prior wound-emission experiment could not accurately analyze 700–720 nm because of its PMT photocathode sensitivity, demonstrating that detector response can limit comparability in the relevant band.

For each wavelength bin, emission-rate density is computed as Jλ=(Cλ-Dλ)/(t·A·Gλ·QEλ·Tλ), where Cλ is sample counts, Dλ is matched dark counts, t is acquisition time, A is emitting area, Gλ is calibrated collection efficiency, QEλ is detector efficiency, and Tλ is optical transmission.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Calibrate both detector paths with the same wavelength-scanned low-flux transfer source, measure beam-splitter ratio and collection geometry, then acquire injured leaves and shuttered dark frames simultaneously. Convert both count streams to photon s^-1 cm^-2 and perform a preregistered paired equivalence test with bounds 0.85–1.15.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Thermoelectrically cooled red-sensitive photon-counting PMT and back-illuminated EMCCD, both characterized from 400 to 870 nm, plus a calibrated beam splitter and tunable low-flux source.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This tests whether a complete calibration chain makes two detector classes agree on absolute wound-induced UPE, rather than advancing another biological stress association already covered by the register.

members.statement: For wounded Arabidopsis thaliana leaves, replacing wavelength-resolved response correction with a single quantum-efficiency value specified at 500 nm will bias the inferred 400–870 nm photon-emission-rate density by at least 25%.

hypothesis.statement: For wounded Arabidopsis thaliana leaves, replacing wavelength-resolved response correction with a single quantum-efficiency value specified at 500 nm will bias the inferred 400–870 nm photon-emission-rate density by at least 25%.

scope.population: Mechanically wounded seven-week-old Arabidopsis thaliana leaves
scope.condition: First 30 minutes after standardized incision following two-hour dark adaptation
scope.comparator: A scalar correction using QE at 500 nm versus correction using measured QE and optical transmission in wavelength bins across 400–870 nm
scope.outcome: Relative error in total photon-emission-rate density and in the estimated 700–870 nm emission fraction

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The absolute relative difference between scalar-QE and wavelength-resolved estimates is less than 25%.
hypothesis.estimand: Absolute calibration bias |Jscalar-Jspectral|/Jspectral.

rationale.step: Wound-induced Arabidopsis emission is spectrally nonuniform and is dominated by 700–750 nm, with additional emission reported from 750–870 nm.
Plant lipid-peroxidation UPE has independently been reported to peak near 680 nm, while another wound study explicitly reported inadequate PMT sensitivity near 700–720 nm.
A human UPE spectrometer study identified wavelength-dependent spectrograph transmission and dark signal as constraints on spectral measurement.
The scalar estimate is Jscalar=Σλ(Cλ-Dλ)/(QE500·T500), whereas the spectral estimate is Jspectral=Σλ(Cλ-Dλ)/(QEλ·Tλ); their relative difference directly quantifies spectral-mismatch bias.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Record injured-leaf emission with a calibrated imaging spectrograph or contiguous bandpass filters, determine end-to-end response at each wavelength using a low-flux source, and process the identical raw observations with scalar and wavelength-resolved corrections.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Back-illuminated cooled EMCCD spectrograph or red-enhanced photon-counting PMT with contiguous bandpass filters, covering 400–870 nm.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This exposes the hidden assumption that one quoted QE can convert broadband counts into photons despite strongly red-weighted biological emission.

members.statement: After two hours of thermal equilibration, cooled PMT dark counts collected over 48 hours will be Poisson-compatible enough that every six-hour block has a Fano factor of 0.8–1.2 and its empirical one-sided 95% blank threshold is no more than 10% above the Poisson-derived threshold.

hypothesis.statement: After two hours of thermal equilibration, cooled PMT dark counts collected over 48 hours will be Poisson-compatible enough that every six-hour block has a Fano factor of 0.8–1.2 and its empirical one-sided 95% blank threshold is no more than 10% above the Poisson-derived threshold.

scope.population: At least three low-dark-count PMT models tested in three light-tight UPE chambers
scope.condition: Fixed gain and detector temperature, two-hour equilibration, followed by continuous 48-hour shuttered acquisition in 60-second bins
scope.comparator: Empirical block-specific blank distribution versus a stationary Poisson model with the same mean
scope.outcome: Fano factor and the ratio of empirical to Poisson one-sided 95% thresholds, also expressed as photon s^-1 cm^-2 after calibration

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: At least one detector has a six-hour block with Fano factor outside 0.8–1.2 or an empirical 95% threshold more than 10% above the Poisson threshold.
hypothesis.estimand: For each detector and block, F=Var(C)/Mean(C) and RLOD=Q0.95,empirical/Q0.95,Poisson.

rationale.step: Dark-count measurements without germinating seeds have been reported to show ordinary rather than anomalous temporal scaling.
Basal and several wound-experiment photocount states have been reported to approximate Poisson distributions.
The UPE review notes that detector dark counts are central to instrument choice and that signal-to-noise ratio of at least one is commonly required.

Fano factor tests dispersion independently of count scale, while the empirical-to-Poisson threshold ratio measures how much a stationary-Poisson assumption understates the blank-defined detection threshold.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Distribute an identical acquisition protocol to three laboratories, log detector and chamber temperatures, acquire continuous shuttered counts, and analyze preregistered six-hour blocks without removing bursts except under explicit hardware-fault rules. Convert thresholds using each detector's wavelength-dependent efficiency and collection geometry.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Thermoelectrically cooled photon-counting PMTs sensitive over approximately 300–800 nm, with electronic shutters, temperature logging, and traceable low-flux efficiency calibration.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This directly tests the stationary-Poisson dark-noise assumption on which many count-subtraction and LOD calculations implicitly depend.

members.statement: For matched astrocyte and glioblastoma cultures containing 10^6 viable cells per well, at least 90% of replicate wells in each cell class will produce a calibrated 350–800 nm emission-rate density whose lower 95% confidence bound exceeds the empirical blank-defined LOD.

hypothesis.statement: For matched astrocyte and glioblastoma cultures containing 10^6 viable cells per well, at least 90% of replicate wells in each cell class will produce a calibrated 350–800 nm emission-rate density whose lower 95% confidence bound exceeds the empirical blank-defined LOD.

scope.population: Cultured astrocytes and glioblastoma cells normalized to 10^6 viable cells per well, with at least 30 wells per class
scope.condition: Fixed medium volume, temperature and dark-adaptation interval, followed by a 30-minute spontaneous-emission measurement
scope.comparator: Cell-free medium wells handled identically and interleaved throughout acquisition
scope.outcome: Fraction of cell-containing wells exceeding an empirical absolute LOD in photon s^-1 cm^-2

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: Fewer than 90% of wells in either cell class have a lower 95% confidence bound above the blank-defined LOD.
hypothesis.estimand: Detection probability in each cell class and the median ratio of net emission-rate density to absolute LOD.

rationale.step: Initial astrocyte and glioblastoma measurements reported clear separation of cellular signals from dark noise using ultra-sensitive photon-counting setups.
That study identifies further optical integration and detector cooling as setup optimizations, indicating that detection performance remains instrument-dependent.
Absolute photon-emission-rate-density LOD is required for direct sensitivity comparison, but is rarely reported in luminescence detection studies.
For each well, the decision statistic is S=(Jcell-Jblank)/LOD; detection requires the lower 95% confidence bound of S to exceed one.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Randomize cell and medium-only wells, interleave shuttered and medium blanks, calibrate end-to-end efficiency and collection geometry, and report both net emission density and a blank-distribution LOD. Repeat the campaign with a PMT and a silicon photon counter.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Low-dark-count cooled PMT and independently calibrated silicon single-photon counter with quartz collection optics covering 350–800 nm.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This converts a reported qualitative separation from dark noise into a preregistered absolute-unit detection claim that another laboratory can directly reproduce.

members.statement: A malignancy classifier trained in one laboratory on calibrated 400–800 nm UPE emission-rate-density time series from a 13-cell-line malignant/non-malignant panel will achieve AUROC of at least 0.80 without model refitting in each of two laboratories using different detector classes.

hypothesis.statement: A malignancy classifier trained in one laboratory on calibrated 400–800 nm UPE emission-rate-density time series from a 13-cell-line malignant/non-malignant panel will achieve AUROC of at least 0.80 without model refitting in each of two laboratories using different detector classes.

scope.population: The 13 human and mouse malignant and non-malignant cell-line panel represented by 10^6 viable cells per plate
scope.condition: Standardized culture, medium, dark adaptation and 100-second acquisition protocol at three laboratories
scope.comparator: External laboratories using detector classes different from the training laboratory, with predictions from the frozen training-laboratory model
scope.outcome: Held-out laboratory AUROC for malignant versus non-malignant classification using absolute time-series and temporal power-density features

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The frozen classifier has AUROC below 0.80 in either external laboratory.
hypothesis.estimand: Minimum AUROC across the two external laboratories, with cell line rather than plate used as the resampling unit.

rationale.step: A 13-cell-line in vitro study reported increased emission from tumor cells and 90% discrimination using temporal spectral-power-density features derived from 100-second photon measurements.
The UPE literature explicitly characterizes the absence of standardization as preventing UPE from becoming a reliable biomarker.
Lack of absolute photon and emission-density LOD reporting precludes direct sensitivity comparison between luminescence instruments.
Each raw bin is transformed to J(t)=[C(t)-D(t)]/[A·G·QEeff·Δt], after which the frozen feature transformation and classifier are applied identically at every laboratory.
The hypothesis is accepted only if both external AUROCs are at least 0.80; taking their minimum prevents a high-performing laboratory from masking a portability failure.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Distribute authenticated cell stocks and a locked acquisition protocol to three laboratories using, respectively, a PMT, EMCCD and silicon photon counter. Calibrate wavelength response, geometry, dark distribution and LOD locally; train once at the designated laboratory; freeze preprocessing and model coefficients; and evaluate blinded external plates without threshold adjustment.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Calibrated photon-counting PMT, back-illuminated EMCCD, or cooled silicon single-photon detector with characterized response across 400–800 nm.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This tests whether absolute calibration makes a published cell-state signal transportable across laboratories and detector classes, rather than merely reproducing within-instrument discrimination.

members.statement: In a single pre-registered diagnostic-accuracy study, a standardized UVA-provocation UPE index (integrated 0-120 s post-irradiation photon count divided by the dark-adapted pre-irradiation baseline on the volar forearm) discriminates a pre-specified redox-abnormal patient group from matched controls with an out-of-sample AUC at least 0.10 higher than spontaneous UPE intensity measured on the same site in the same session.

hypothesis.statement: In a single pre-registered diagnostic-accuracy study, a standardized UVA-provocation UPE index (integrated 0-120 s post-irradiation photon count divided by the dark-adapted pre-irradiation baseline on the volar forearm) discriminates a pre-specified redox-abnormal patient group from matched controls with an out-of-sample AUC at least 0.10 higher than spontaneous UPE intensity measured on the same site in the same session.

scope.population: Adults 18-65 with one pre-specified systemic redox disorder (erythropoietic protoporphyria or early-stage type 2 diabetes), plus controls matched on age, sex and Fitzpatrick skin type; n >= 100 per arm, split 60/40 into a training and a single-use held-out set.
scope.condition: One session per subject: 20 min standardized dark adaptation, volar forearm, spontaneous UPE recorded for 600 s, then a radiometer-verified 365 nm UVA dose (5 J/cm2) followed by 120 s provoked recording; classifier specification locked and registered before unblinding.
scope.comparator: Spontaneous (unprovoked) UPE intensity from the identical site, subject, session and detector - a within-subject head-to-head, not a cross-study comparison.
scope.outcome: Area under the ROC curve on the held-out set, evaluated once, for each of the two locked classifiers.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: Delta-AUC (provoked minus spontaneous) is <= 0, or its upper 95% CI bound lies below 0.10 - i.e. provocation buys no discriminative advantage over the spontaneous intensity on which nearly all existing clinical UPE claims rest.
hypothesis.estimand: Delta-AUC = AUC(provocation index) - AUC(spontaneous intensity), with 95% CI from a paired DeLong test on the held-out set.

rationale.step: A within-study dissociation between spontaneous and provoked UPE already exists in the corpus: in erythropoietic protoporphyria patients, spontaneous UPE resembled that of healthy individuals, while the post-solar-simulated-light initial burst correlated with plasma iron and erythrocyte protoporphyrin IX and was suppressed by oral zinc. Spontaneous emission carried no disease information; provoked emission did.

UVA-provoked UPE is the only human UPE readout in the corpus that has been shown to move dose-dependently with a controlled intervention in formal clinical trials (two trials, 20 volunteers each, dose-dependent antioxidant effect of topical vitamin C and alpha-glucosylrutin), and the same work qualifies UVA-provoked UPE explicitly as a validated non-invasive method.

Spontaneous human skin UPE is on the order of tens to hundreds of photons per second per square centimetre, whereas UV provocation raises skin emission by a factor that scales with UV dose and is suppressible by antioxidants - i.e. the provoked signal sits far above the spontaneous one on the same detector.

Photon-shot-noise calculation of the SNR gain: take spontaneous emission s = 10 detected counts/s (100 photons/s/cm2 over 1 cm2 at ~10% end-to-end detection efficiency) against a background b = 10 counts/s, integrated for T = 100 s. SNR = sT/sqrt((s+b)T) = 1000/sqrt(2000) = 22.4. A provocation that raises the emission tenfold gives s = 100 counts/s: SNR = 10000/sqrt(11000) = 95.3. The provoked acquisition delivers a ~4.3-fold SNR gain at fixed integration time, which for a fixed true group separation propagates directly into higher attainable discrimination.

The field's own analytical review recommends populations of approximately 50-100 subjects for human UPE studies, so the n >= 100 per arm specified here is the smallest sample the field itself would accept as adequate.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Pre-registered two-arm diagnostic accuracy study. Each participant is measured once spontaneously (600 s) and once after a calibrated 365 nm UVA dose on the volar forearm, in a single light-tight session with capped-detector and empty-chamber background runs bracketing every acquisition. Two classifiers (spontaneous intensity; provocation index) are specified, trained and frozen on the 60% training split, then evaluated exactly once on the 40% held-out split, with the paired Delta-AUC as the pre-specified primary endpoint.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Cooled low-noise bialkali photomultiplier in photon-counting mode, 300-650 nm, in a light-tight chamber; calibrated 365 nm UVA LED source with radiometer-verified irradiance; per-session capped-detector and empty-chamber dark runs.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: Register claim H8 asks whether surface UPE adds predictive power beyond physiological covariates; it does not ask which acquisition modality carries the information. This claim makes the modality itself the estimand and predicts that spontaneous intensity - the readout underlying essentially every clinical UPE claim on the register - loses head-to-head to a provocation-response index, with an existing within-study dissociation (EPP) as the seed observation.

members.statement: For the clinical classification tasks in the corpus that are performed with room-lit RGB/multispectral cameras or corona-discharge (GDV/electro-photonic) devices, adding a true dark-chamber single-photon-counting UPE measurement of the same anatomical site contributes no discriminative information (Delta-AUC <= 0.05), because those devices record reflected or discharge-generated light and not endogenous photon emission.

hypothesis.statement: For the clinical classification tasks in the corpus that are performed with room-lit RGB/multispectral cameras or corona-discharge (GDV/electro-photonic) devices, adding a true dark-chamber single-photon-counting UPE measurement of the same anatomical site contributes no discriminative information (Delta-AUC <= 0.05), because those devices record reflected or discharge-generated light and not endogenous photon emission.

scope.population: Patients with carpal tunnel syndrome confirmed by nerve conduction testing plus matched controls, replicating the cohort design of the NEV-camera study; n >= 100 total.
scope.condition: Every hand measured three ways within one session: (a) NEV-class RGB multispectral camera under specified room illumination with lux logged, (b) Bio-Well-class GDV/electro-photonic fingertip imaging, (c) EMCCD photon counting of the same palmar field in a light-tight chamber after 20 min dark adaptation.
scope.comparator: The locked RGB + GDV feature classifier alone, i.e. the published instrument classes without any photon-counting input.
scope.outcome: Held-out AUC of the combined classifier minus the held-out AUC of the RGB + GDV classifier, plus the directly measured photon flux ratio between the room-lit and dark-chamber conditions on the same skin.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: Delta-AUC > 0.05 with the lower 95% CI bound above 0.05 - i.e. genuine endogenous photon emission does carry clinical information that the reflectance and discharge devices miss, and the instrument-class objection fails.
hypothesis.estimand: Delta-AUC on the single-use held-out split, with 95% bootstrap CI; secondary estimand is the measured ratio of detected photon flux (room-lit reflectance : dark-chamber emission) from the identical skin field.

rationale.step: The carpal tunnel study that supplies the corpus's highest reported clinical accuracy for a 'biophotonic' device (93.33% SVM accuracy, 81.79% cross-validated) explicitly derives its features from skin texture and colour variation in RGB multispectral images, and its own text distances the method from subtle-energy-field claims. The measured quantity is reflectance under illumination, not emission in darkness.

The electro-photonic emission analysis literature grouped with UPE as clinical evidence uses a certified Bio-Well GDV Camera 2.0 to image light generated by a high-voltage gas discharge at the fingertip in an open, non-randomized study of 56 respondents; a second corpus work uses the same EPI/GDV modality alongside EEG. Corona-discharge luminescence is externally driven, orders of magnitude brighter than UPE, and is not spontaneous emission.
Spontaneous human skin UPE is quantified in the corpus at tens to hundreds of photons per second per square centimetre, which fixes the scale of the quantity these devices would have to detect.

Order-of-magnitude computation of the reflectance-to-emission ratio: 100 lux of room light at 555 nm equals 100/683 = 0.146 W/m2 = 1.46e-5 W/cm2. At a 555 nm photon energy of 3.58e-19 J, that is 4.1e13 photons/s/cm2 incident on the skin. At ~30% diffuse skin reflectance, ~1.2e13 photons/s/cm2 reach the camera, versus ~1e2 photons/s/cm2 of endogenous UPE - a ratio of ~1.2e11. Any room-lit RGB image is more than ten orders of magnitude dominated by reflected illumination, so no UPE component is recoverable from it even in principle.

A photon-counting arm capable of the required sensitivity is available and demonstrated on living animals: EMCCD and CCD cameras with >90% quantum efficiency capture single visible photons at low noise and resolve live-versus-dead contrast in mice, so the null arm of this experiment is technically decisive rather than underpowered.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Three-modality, same-session study on one locked clinical task (CTS vs control), with feature sets, model class and split pre-registered and the held-out set evaluated once. In parallel, use the EMCCD to measure absolute detected photon flux from the same hand field (i) under the RGB camera's illumination and (ii) in the light-tight chamber, and report the measured ratio against the calculated 1e11 prediction. The instrument-provenance audit is the primary deliverable: which detected photons actually carry the classification.
hypothesis.required_instrument: EMCCD, >90% QE, 400-900 nm, in a light-tight chamber with capped-detector dark runs; NEV-class RGB multispectral camera and Bio-Well-class GDV device as published; calibrated lux meter and traceable low-level light source for the flux comparison.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This exposes a hidden assumption that the register's entire L6 clinical branch (H8, and the diagnostic literature feeding it) depends on: that the accuracies cited as evidence for 'UPE as clinical biomarker' were obtained with instruments physically capable of detecting UPE. No register claim addresses instrument-class provenance, and the corpus's two highest-profile recent clinical-support results (NEV camera, GDV) are both non-UPE modalities.

members.statement: Clamping the measured skin site to a fixed temperature (32.0 +/- 0.2 C) through a transparent thermostatted window removes at least half of the between-state difference in human surface UPE reported for affective and meditative state manipulations, and the attenuation is larger for detectors whose spectral window extends beyond 650 nm than for detectors restricted to 300-650 nm.

hypothesis.statement: Clamping the measured skin site to a fixed temperature (32.0 +/- 0.2 C) through a transparent thermostatted window removes at least half of the between-state difference in human surface UPE reported for affective and meditative state manipulations, and the attenuation is larger for detectors whose spectral window extends beyond 650 nm than for detectors restricted to 300-650 nm.

scope.population: Healthy adults 18-65, n >= 60, no dermatological disease at the measured site.
scope.condition: Within-subject crossover: two state conditions (guided relaxation vs. an arousal task of the anger-induction or breathwork type used in the corpus), each measured twice - once with the dorsal hand at free skin temperature and once with the site thermostatted at 32.0 +/- 0.2 C behind a fused-silica window - with condition order randomized and calibrated IR thermography of the site logged throughout.
scope.comparator: The free-skin-temperature arm of the same subject and the same state contrast; and, in parallel, the bialkali (300-650 nm) versus extended-red multialkali (300-850 nm) detector.
scope.outcome: Standardized effect size of the state contrast on integrated hand UPE, computed separately for each temperature arm and each detector band.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The thermostatted effect size is >= 80% of the free-temperature effect size (its lower 95% CI bound above 0.8 of it), i.e. skin temperature is a benign additive covariate rather than the generator of the reported state effects - which would kill this hypothesis and support H12/H8 as stated.
hypothesis.estimand: Ratio of state-contrast effect sizes, d(thermostatted)/d(free), with 95% CI; secondary estimand is the partial correlation between UPE and skin temperature with state regressed out, reported per detector band.

rationale.step: In exactly the meditation/breathwork paradigm used to claim state-dependent human UPE, a 2026 multi-sensor feasibility study reports moderate within-subject correlation (r > 0.4) between infrared nose temperature and left-hand UPE, alongside strong correlations (r > 0.5) between UPE from the two hands. Thermal state and the UPE readout co-vary within the very design that attributes the change to the mental state.

Skin temperature is an established modulator of the UPE signal itself, not merely of the physiology behind it: the validation study that qualified UVA-provoked UPE as a clinical method identified skin temperature, skin humidity and ambient O2 concentration as critical parameters affecting both quality and quantity of the signal, with UVA-induced UPE decreasing as temperature rose.

Claims that human surface/head UPE reports internal state have already been shown to be vulnerable to background-light contamination and to detector spectral response: photons below 600 nm are strongly attenuated by tissue while longer wavelengths fall largely outside PMT sensitivity, so the residual signal in a red-extended detector is precisely where a thermal/optical artifact would sit.

The field's own 2026 biomarker review names susceptibility to thermal and optical confounds, together with the absence of standardized clinical measurement protocols, as the key experimental constraints on UPE as a candidate biomarker - so this is the field's stated blocker, stated by the same source that frames Q6.

Identifiability argument: the published state-contrast studies (e.g. the nine-volunteer anger proof-of-concept) report relative intensity changes with no thermostatting and no temperature covariate. State manipulations that alter peripheral vasomotor tone move hand skin temperature by several degrees C, so in those designs the redox-driven and temperature-driven components are not merely unmeasured, they are structurally unidentified: no post-hoc statistical adjustment can separate them, and only an intervention that fixes temperature can.

The anger-induction proof of concept is the corpus's clearest instance of an uncontrolled state contrast: nine volunteers, CCD imaging of the upper body, relative intensity higher during induced anger than during relaxation, with the authors themselves calling for replication at larger n.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Randomized crossover with a fused-silica thermostatted contact window over the dorsal hand, calibrated IR thermography of the same field, and two photon-counting channels run in parallel on a beamsplit field (bialkali 300-650 nm; extended-red multialkali 300-850 nm). Primary endpoint is the ratio of state-contrast effect sizes between thermostatted and free arms; secondary endpoint is whether that ratio differs between the two spectral channels, which discriminates a physiological temperature effect from a detector-side red/NIR artifact.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Two photon-counting PMTs - bialkali 300-650 nm and extended-red multialkali 300-850 nm - on a split field in a light-tight room; calibrated 8-14 micron IR camera; Peltier-thermostatted fused-silica contact window; capped-detector and empty-chamber background runs bracketing every acquisition.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: Register claim H8 lists skin temperature as a covariate to be adjusted for and H12 treats state effects as a live anomalous claim. This hypothesis asserts that temperature is not an additive nuisance but the generating mechanism of the reported state effects, and it specifies the only design that can identify that - physically clamping the temperature rather than regressing on it - plus a dual-band contrast that separates a physiological from a detector-side origin. Neither the intervention nor the band-dependence prediction is on the register.

members.statement: A two-band UPE intensity ratio (I(>550 nm)/I(>495 nm), or I(610-630 nm)/I(395-455 nm)) trained as a clinical classifier at one laboratory transfers to an independent laboratory with different photomultiplier and filter hardware losing less than half the AUC that an absolute-intensity classifier loses on the same transfer, in the same pre-specified clinical task.

hypothesis.statement: A two-band UPE intensity ratio (I(>550 nm)/I(>495 nm), or I(610-630 nm)/I(395-455 nm)) trained as a clinical classifier at one laboratory transfers to an independent laboratory with different photomultiplier and filter hardware losing less than half the AUC that an absolute-intensity classifier loses on the same transfer, in the same pre-specified clinical task.

scope.population: One pre-specified clinical contrast - acute upper-respiratory infection versus healthy, the contrast for which the corpus already reports a working spectral ratio - measured at two independent laboratories with different PMT and filter hardware; n >= 80 per site.
scope.condition: Fingertip/two-hand UPE with a motorized cut-off and bandpass filter wheel, identical written acquisition protocol at both sites, no cross-site recalibration, no site-specific retraining; site A model frozen and registered before any site B data are unblinded.
scope.comparator: The absolute-intensity classifier built from the same acquisitions at site A, transferred identically.
scope.outcome: Transfer AUC loss for each classifier, defined as AUC(internal, site A held-out) minus AUC(external, site B).

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The ratio classifier's transfer loss is >= 50% of the intensity classifier's transfer loss (lower CI bound above 0.5 of it), i.e. band ratios are no more portable across instruments than absolute intensity, and spectral features buy no transferability.
hypothesis.estimand: The ratio of transfer AUC losses, Delta-AUC(ratio)/Delta-AUC(intensity), with bootstrap 95% CI; reported alongside both internal and external AUCs for each classifier.

rationale.step: Spectral ratios, not absolute intensities, are already the discriminating feature in two independent UPE studies in the corpus: the photon emission ratio between 550 nm and 495 nm cut-off filters separated cold patients from healthy subjects using a two-hand fingertip system, and the 610-630/395-455 nm spectral ratio tracked the logarithm of tumour volume in a breast-cancer-bearing mouse model (R2 = 0.947 at the lesion site, 0.892 at the healthy site).

Band ratios have a mechanistic referent rather than being an arbitrary engineered feature: UVA-induced UPE from skin shows biomolecule-specific spectral patterns (linoleic and linolenic acid, elastin, phospholipids, DHICA), and the skin tissue spectrum is a superposition of these distinct emitters, so a ratio between two bands reports a shift in which emitter dominates.

Absolute UPE intensity is documented to be non-transferable: it differs between subjects and between hand locations, fluctuates over the 24 h cycle with the dorsal side varying more than the palm, changes left-right symmetry across the day, and carries additional 14-day, 1-month, 3-month and 9-month rhythms plus a whole-body diurnal rhythm. Every one of these is a multiplicative nuisance on the intensity scale.

Variance derivation for why a same-detector ratio should transfer better. Write the measured band intensities as log I1 = log a + log g + n1 and log I2 = log b + log g + n2, where g collects all multiplicative nuisances common to both bands measured through the same optical train (collection solid angle, source-detector distance, gain drift, dark-adaptation-dependent scaling, subject-level scaling). Then log R = log I1 - log I2 removes log g exactly. Across sites, Var(log R) = Var(log I1) + Var(log I2) - 2 Cov(log I1, log I2), which is strictly less than min(Var(log I1), Var(log I2)) whenever the cross-band correlation exceeds 0.5 and the band variances are comparable - the regime that common-mode nuisance dominance implies. The residual cross-site term is only the band-differential filter/QE response, which is directly measurable against a traceable calibrated source.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Two-site external validation with hardware-blind protocol transfer. Site A collects, trains and freezes two classifiers (two-band ratio; absolute intensity) with a registered analysis plan; site B collects under the same written protocol on different hardware and the frozen models are applied once. Per-band throughput at both sites is measured against a traceable calibrated low-level light source and reported, so any residual ratio drift can be attributed to filter/QE rather than biology. Primary endpoint is the ratio of transfer losses.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Photon-counting PMT with a motorized cut-off/bandpass filter wheel covering 395-455, 495, 550 and 610-630 nm, at both sites; traceable calibrated low-level light source for per-band throughput characterization; light-tight chamber with per-session capped and empty background runs.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: Register claim H11 asserts that UPE spectral distribution carries state-specific information beyond total intensity. That is an information claim inside one laboratory. This converts it into the property that actually decides clinical adoption - portability across instruments and sites - and states a specific, falsifiable ordering of transfer losses with a variance derivation behind it. No register claim mentions cross-site transfer, which is the step at which candidate biomarkers usually die.

members.statement: At least half of the nose/glabella-versus-cheek UPE intensity contrast in human facial skin originates in the removable skin-surface lipid film and its microbial porphyrins rather than in viable epidermal or dermal cells, such that a single standardized degreasing wipe abolishes >= 50% of that regional contrast.

hypothesis.statement: At least half of the nose/glabella-versus-cheek UPE intensity contrast in human facial skin originates in the removable skin-surface lipid film and its microbial porphyrins rather than in viable epidermal or dermal cells, such that a single standardized degreasing wipe abolishes >= 50% of that regional contrast.

scope.population: Healthy adults 20-60 with a measurable baseline facial porphyrin score, n >= 40, no acne treatment or topical antimicrobial in the preceding 8 weeks.
scope.condition: Within-subject split-face: one hemiface receives a standardized lipid-solvent degreasing wipe, the other a sham wipe; UPE imaged before and 10 min after. Arm 2 repeats the imaging after 4 weeks of split-face topical antimicrobial versus vehicle.
scope.comparator: The sham-wiped / vehicle-treated hemiface of the same subject at the same session, same camera, same dark adaptation.
scope.outcome: The (nose + glabella) minus cheek UPE intensity contrast measured by cryogenic CCD imaging, and the correlation between UPE intensity and facial porphyrin score.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: Degreasing and 4-week antimicrobial treatment reduce the regional contrast by less than 50% (upper 95% CI bound below 50%), i.e. the regional facial UPE pattern is generated in living epidermis/dermis and surface lipid is not the dominant source.
hypothesis.estimand: Fractional reduction in the (nose+glabella - cheek) UPE contrast, treated versus sham, with 95% CI; secondary estimand is the change in the UPE-porphyrin-score correlation coefficient after treatment.

rationale.step: Facial UPE imaging localizes the highest intensity to the nose, its surrounding regions and the area between the eyebrows, and finds UPE intensity correlated with skin porphyrin score while showing no correlation with skin colour parameters. Those are precisely the sebaceous, porphyrin-producing regions, and the porphyrin association is the strongest reported covariate.

The skin surface lipid film is a sebum plus keratinocyte-membrane mixture uniquely rich in squalene, continuously oxidatively modified by resident and pathological microbial metabolism and by UV, generating reactive peroxidation by-products - i.e. an extracellular, UPE-competent oxidation compartment sitting on top of the tissue the assay is intended to interrogate.

The accepted final emitters of skin UPE are triplet carbonyls and singlet oxygen produced by ROS-driven lipid and protein oxidation, and skin UPE is a superposition of light from several biomolecular emitters. Those same reactions run in surface lipid exactly as in cells, so intensity and geometry alone cannot attribute the emission to a living compartment.

The competing account is explicit in the corpus - CCD imaging with antioxidant suppression indicates UPE is generated not only from the epidermis but also from the dermis - and it makes the opposite prediction for this experiment: a surface-only manipulation should leave the regional contrast intact. The two accounts are therefore directly separable by one intervention.

Identification argument for why degreasing is the right instrument: the surface lipid film is the only UPE-competent compartment that can be removed in seconds without changing perfusion, skin temperature, cell viability or the optical geometry of the measurement. Every other way of suppressing a compartment (antioxidant application, occlusion, cooling) alters at least one of those and reintroduces the confounds this experiment is meant to exclude. A sham-wiped hemiface controls for the mechanical and thermal perturbation of wiping itself.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Split-face, sham-controlled study. Cryogenic CCD UPE imaging of the full face before and 10 min after a standardized lipid-solvent degreasing wipe on one randomly assigned hemiface; region-of-interest analysis over nose, glabella and cheek. Repeat after 4 weeks of split-face topical antimicrobial versus vehicle. Facial porphyrin score by standard UV-fluorescence imaging at each timepoint, plus skin surface temperature to confirm the wipe did not shift it. Primary endpoint is the fractional collapse of the regional contrast.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Cryogenic full-frame back-illuminated CCD imaging system, 400-700 nm, in a light-tight room (the class used for facial UPE imaging in the corpus); standard UV-fluorescence facial porphyrin imaging; contact thermometry of each ROI.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: Register claim H4a attributes UPE to ROS-driven lipid/protein oxidation without asking in which compartment, and H8 presumes surface UPE reports a systemic state. This exposes the compartment assumption both depend on: if the dominant regional signal comes from a wipe-removable extracorporeal lipid/microbial film, human surface UPE is a skin-surface-lipid assay rather than a systemic biomarker, and any clinical validation that does not standardize degreasing is measuring grooming. The register contains no compartment-attribution claim and no surface-removal experiment.

members.statement: Same-clock-time, 4-week test-retest reliability of standardized dorsal-hand spontaneous UPE intensity in healthy adults has ICC(2,1) below 0.6, which caps the out-of-sample AUC of any single-session intensity-based classifier below 0.80 even when the true group separation is a large standardized difference of 1.5.

hypothesis.statement: Same-clock-time, 4-week test-retest reliability of standardized dorsal-hand spontaneous UPE intensity in healthy adults has ICC(2,1) below 0.6, which caps the out-of-sample AUC of any single-session intensity-based classifier below 0.80 even when the true group separation is a large standardized difference of 1.5.

scope.population: Healthy adults 18-65, n >= 50, no acute illness, stable medication, no intervention of any kind during the study.
scope.condition: Five sessions at weekly intervals, each at the same clock time (+/- 30 min), identical 20 min dark adaptation, identical detector-to-skin geometry, dorsal left and right hand, 600 s integration, with capped-detector and empty-chamber background runs at every session.
scope.comparator: None - this is a reliability study; the comparator is the reliability threshold the field's own reported single-session accuracies implicitly require.
scope.outcome: ICC(2,1) of the 600 s integrated photon count, its standard error of measurement, and the minimal detectable change.

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: ICC(2,1) >= 0.75 with lower 95% CI bound above 0.6 - i.e. spontaneous UPE intensity is a reliable individual-level quantity and the attenuation ceiling does not bind, which kills this hypothesis.
hypothesis.estimand: ICC(2,1) with 95% CI, and the derived attenuation-implied maximum achievable AUC, AUC_max = Phi(d_true * sqrt(ICC) / sqrt(2)), reported for d_true = 1.0 and 1.5.

rationale.step: Spontaneous human hand UPE fluctuates systematically within 24 h, with mean emission differing both between subjects and between hand locations, greater fluctuation on the dorsal than the palmar side, no apparent correlation between palm and dorsal fluctuations, and a change in left-right symmetry across the day on the dorsal side - i.e. the exact site and readout used for clinical claims is the least stable one.

Whole-body UPE follows a diurnal rhythm imaged with a cryogenic CCD, and long-run daily human skin measurements report additional 14-day, 1-month, 3-month and 9-month rhythms. Week-scale drift is therefore expected by the field's own descriptive literature, not an anomaly to be designed away.

No test-retest reliability coefficient for human UPE appears anywhere in the retrieved corpus. The closest is a 2025 human measurement protocol that uses the coefficient of variation as a proxy for signal variability - a quantity that pools between-subject and within-subject variance and therefore cannot yield a reliability coefficient or an attenuation ceiling.

Attenuation computation fixing the ceiling. For X = T + e with reliability rho = Var(T)/Var(X), an observed standardized group difference attenuates as d_obs = d_true * sqrt(rho), and for normal equal-variance groups AUC = Phi(d_obs / sqrt(2)). At rho = 0.6 and d_true = 1.5: d_obs = 1.5 * 0.7746 = 1.162, AUC = Phi(0.8216) = 0.794 < 0.80. At rho = 0.6 and d_true = 1.0: AUC = Phi(0.548) = 0.708. At rho = 0.4 and d_true = 1.0: AUC = Phi(0.447) = 0.673. Any single-session single-feature intensity classifier reporting held-out AUC above these values, given a measured rho in this range, is reporting overfitting or leakage rather than signal - which makes the reliability coefficient a pre-emptive audit on the entire published accuracy record.

The field asks for larger populations, better statistical tools, and validation of biophotonic measurement techniques as objective biomarkers, but neither its analytical review nor its 2026 biomarker review names measurement reliability as the prerequisite that bounds all of it; the 2026 review instead cites thermal/optical confounds and the absence of standardized clinical protocols.

The background discipline needed for this study is already specified in the corpus: capped-detector dark count runs and no-participant background runs must bracket the participant acquisition, because reported human UPE magnitudes have been shown to be explicable by background light contamination when that discipline is absent.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Five-session, no-intervention reliability study on the identical rig, site and protocol that a subsequent diagnostic study would use. Report ICC(2,1), SEM and minimal detectable change for the 600 s integrated count, for each hand and side, and publish the attenuation-implied AUC ceiling for that rig as a pre-registered constraint on any accuracy the same rig later reports. Run capped-detector and empty-chamber background acquisitions at every session and report their drift alongside the biological drift, so instrument instability and biological instability are separated.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Cooled low-noise photon-counting PMT, 300-650 nm, moveable head with fixed reproducible detector-to-skin geometry, in a light-tight dark room; per-session capped-detector and empty-chamber background runs; logged room temperature, humidity and skin surface temperature.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: The register contains no reliability claim of any kind, yet every one of its L5/L6 claims (H3, H8, H9, H12) silently assumes the measurement is reliable enough to carry the predictive load it is assigned. This makes the reliability ceiling itself the estimand, derives the exact AUC bound it implies, and is the cheapest experiment on this list - one no-intervention study that would either license or pre-emptively invalidate a whole class of reported single-session accuracies before any clinical validation is funded.

members.statement: In adults spanning the full range of skin pigmentation, calibrated 350–650 nm UPE emitted 1–3 minutes after a standardized suberythemal UVA exposure will add at least 0.10 to out-of-sample R² for predicting 24-hour erythema beyond UVA dose, baseline erythema, skin lightness, skin temperature and perfusion.

hypothesis.statement: In adults spanning the full range of skin pigmentation, calibrated 350–650 nm UPE emitted 1–3 minutes after a standardized suberythemal UVA exposure will add at least 0.10 to out-of-sample R² for predicting 24-hour erythema beyond UVA dose, baseline erythema, skin lightness, skin temperature and perfusion.

scope.population: Adults with prospectively balanced skin-lightness strata
scope.condition: Standardized suberythemal solar-simulated UVA exposure after controlled acclimation and dark adaptation
scope.comparator: Prediction model containing UVA dose, baseline colorimetry, skin lightness L*, temperature and perfusion but no UPE
scope.outcome: Change in colorimeter-measured erythema a* at 24 hours

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The cross-validated incremental R² from adding 1–3-minute UPE is less than 0.10, or its bootstrap 95% confidence interval includes zero.
hypothesis.estimand: ΔR² = R²clinical+UPE − R²clinical in a locked external-validation cohort.

rationale.step: UV-induced UPE averaged over 1–3 minutes increased with dose and was highly correlated with cutaneous redness 24 hours later; accompanying cell experiments linked the signal to lipid peroxidation.
UVA-induced UPE depends on skin lightness and persists for up to two hours, making pigmentation a load-bearing covariate rather than a demographic nuisance variable.
Clinical UPE measurement is vulnerable to thermal and optical confounds and lacks standardized protocols.
For each held-out participant, compute predictions from nested models and calculate ΔR²; the hypothesis survives only if ΔR²≥0.10 and the participant-bootstrap 95% confidence interval excludes zero.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Pre-register a multicentre dose-response study with a locked acquisition window, sham-exposed neighboring skin, photon-reference calibration, blinded 24-hour colorimetry and a completely held-out validation centre; fit the clinical model first and add only the pre-specified background-subtracted 1–3-minute photon radiance.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Calibrated photon-counting photomultiplier or cooled EMCCD covering 350–650 nm in a light-tight chamber, plus a skin colorimeter, thermometer and perfusion monitor.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This advances beyond H8 by testing a provoked, temporally fixed UPE measurement against a future clinical photodamage endpoint across pigmentation strata rather than associating baseline surface UPE with generic systemic oxidative status.

members.statement: In adults with type 2 diabetes starting a glucose-lowering regimen, the week-2 change in the hand-UPE photon-count ratio 495–550 nm/550–610 nm will add at least 0.10 to out-of-sample R² for predicting 12-week HbA1c reduction beyond baseline HbA1c, medication class, BMI and total UPE intensity.

hypothesis.statement: In adults with type 2 diabetes starting a glucose-lowering regimen, the week-2 change in the hand-UPE photon-count ratio 495–550 nm/550–610 nm will add at least 0.10 to out-of-sample R² for predicting 12-week HbA1c reduction beyond baseline HbA1c, medication class, BMI and total UPE intensity.

scope.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes initiating or intensifying a stable glucose-lowering regimen
scope.condition: Bilateral hand UPE measured before treatment and at week 2 under identical circadian, dark-adaptation and environmental conditions
scope.comparator: Clinical prediction model using baseline HbA1c, medication class, BMI and broadband UPE intensity without the spectral ratio
scope.outcome: Laboratory-measured change in HbA1c from baseline to week 12

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: Adding the week-2 spectral-ratio change produces incremental cross-validated R² below 0.10 or a 95% confidence interval including zero.
hypothesis.estimand: Incremental external-validation R² attributable to Δlog[(495–550 nm counts)/(550–610 nm counts)].

rationale.step: In treated type 2 diabetes patients, UPE intensity changed over two weeks and the 495–550 nm/550–610 nm ratio was negatively correlated with contemporaneous syndrome scores.
Separate human studies report UPE differences between people with type 2 diabetes and healthy controls and propose UPE for early-stage diabetes detection.
Plasma metabolomics work in pre-diabetes linked UPE-based subtyping to lipid-profile differences, providing a biochemical candidate source of diabetes-related optical variation.
An analytical review specifically recommends combining spectral information with intensity, using larger populations and applying statistical validation.

Calculate the log spectral ratio at both visits, subtract baseline from week 2, and compare locked nested models in held-out patients; ΔR²≥0.10 with a positive lower confidence bound is the decision rule.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Run a pre-registered prospective cohort alongside routine diabetes treatment, with fixed hand sites and blinded HbA1c assays; train the model in two clinics and test it without refitting in a third clinic.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Calibrated cooled photon-counting PMT with 495–550 nm and 550–610 nm bandpass channels plus a 400–650 nm broadband channel.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: The registered claims do not test whether an early UPE spectral change forecasts a later objective biochemical treatment response; this replaces contemporaneous subjective syndrome correlation with prospective HbA1c prediction.

members.statement: In patients with erythropoietic protoporphyria, the calibrated initial 350–650 nm UPE burst following a standardized low-dose solar-simulated exposure will improve prediction of the 24-hour phototoxic skin reaction by at least 0.10 AUC beyond erythrocyte protoporphyrin IX, plasma iron, exposure dose and skin lightness.

hypothesis.statement: In patients with erythropoietic protoporphyria, the calibrated initial 350–650 nm UPE burst following a standardized low-dose solar-simulated exposure will improve prediction of the 24-hour phototoxic skin reaction by at least 0.10 AUC beyond erythrocyte protoporphyrin IX, plasma iron, exposure dose and skin lightness.

scope.population: Adolescents and adults with biochemically or genetically confirmed erythropoietic protoporphyria
scope.condition: Dermatologist-supervised low-dose solar-simulated exposure of a fixed skin site, measured before and during routine treatment
scope.comparator: Clinical model containing erythrocyte PPIX, plasma iron, exposure dose and L* but no UPE
scope.outcome: Pre-specified 24-hour phototoxic reaction defined by blinded erythema colorimetry and a standardized pain threshold

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The UPE-augmented model improves externally validated AUC by less than 0.10 or has a non-positive lower 95% confidence bound.
hypothesis.estimand: ΔAUC = AUCclinical+initial-burst-UPE − AUCclinical for the pre-specified 24-hour phototoxic-reaction endpoint.

rationale.step: EPP involves PPIX accumulation and acute photosensitivity; in 14 patients, the post-exposure initial UPE burst correlated with plasma iron and erythrocyte PPIX and varied inversely with plasma zinc during treatment.
In human skin generally, early post-UV UPE predicted 24-hour erythema and tracked lipid-peroxidation-related photodamage.
Skin lightness materially affects UVA-induced UPE and therefore must be included in the comparator model.
Compute each model's patient-level ROC curve in a held-out centre; subtract AUCs and bootstrap by patient, declaring support only for ΔAUC≥0.10 with a positive lower confidence bound.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Pre-register a repeated-measures dermatology study using a safe dose ladder, fixed anatomical site, sham-exposed control site and blinded 24-hour assessment; lock the initial-burst integration window before enrollment and validate the model at a second EPP centre.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Calibrated photon-counting PMT covering 350–650 nm with second-scale acquisition in a light-tight skin chamber, plus colorimetry and a calibrated solar simulator.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This tests whether UPE adds clinically actionable prediction beyond the established PPIX and iron measurements, rather than merely correlating UPE with those laboratory variables or with generic oxidative status.

members.statement: In first-ever unilateral ischemic stroke with upper-limb paresis, the simultaneous affected/unaffected hand UPE ratio measured within 14 days will add at least 0.10 to out-of-sample R² for 90-day upper-limb motor recovery beyond baseline motor score, lesion burden, skin temperature and perfusion.

hypothesis.statement: In first-ever unilateral ischemic stroke with upper-limb paresis, the simultaneous affected/unaffected hand UPE ratio measured within 14 days will add at least 0.10 to out-of-sample R² for 90-day upper-limb motor recovery beyond baseline motor score, lesion burden, skin temperature and perfusion.

scope.population: Adults with first-ever unilateral ischemic stroke and measurable upper-limb paresis, plus age-matched neurologically healthy controls
scope.condition: Simultaneous bilateral palmar measurement within 14 days of stroke after environmental acclimation and dark adaptation
scope.comparator: Prognostic model containing baseline Fugl–Meyer Upper Extremity score, imaging-derived lesion burden, skin temperature and perfusion but no UPE ratio
scope.outcome: Change in Fugl–Meyer Upper Extremity score from baseline to day 90

hypothesis.null_hypothesis: The affected/unaffected UPE ratio contributes less than 0.10 incremental external-validation R² or its coefficient is unstable in sign across validation sites.
hypothesis.estimand: Incremental R² for 90-day Fugl–Meyer improvement plus the cross-site sign consistency of the log affected/unaffected photon-radiance ratio.

rationale.step: Year-long bilateral measurements found relatively preserved left-right balance in healthy people but reported severe imbalance in some stroke patients using two PMTs spanning 300–650 nm.
Human UPE displays a diurnal rhythm, so sequential left-right measurements could convert time drift into apparent pathological asymmetry.
Human hand UPE varies by surface and individual, with palmar measurements reported as less variable in an analytical review, supporting a simultaneous within-person palmar ratio.
Calculate log(UPEaffected/UPEunaffected), add it to the locked clinical model and evaluate ΔR² in a held-out hospital; support requires ΔR²≥0.10 and the same coefficient direction at every site.

hypothesis.proposed_experiment: Use paired detectors to measure both palms concurrently at baseline, repeat at discharge for reliability, and obtain blinded day-90 motor scores; train across two stroke units and validate without recalibration at a third.
hypothesis.required_instrument: Two spectrally matched, calibrated photon-counting PMTs covering 300–650 nm with identical apertures and simultaneous acquisition, plus skin temperature and laser-Doppler perfusion sensors.
hypothesis.novelty_self_claim: This converts an old cross-sectional asymmetry observation into a prospective, within-person prognostic endpoint and explicitly tests the hidden assumption that asymmetry is not sequential-measurement or perfusion artifact.
